texto: ### Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)
texto: - **Hard key on the working hand** [Detail/Pressure]: single hard source 45° camera-side onto knuckles on the shifter — finger shadows rake the skin, sweat reads as discrete specular dots, veins as ridges, background crushed. The whitening knuckle IS the fear.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)
texto: - **Backlight / rim on metal edge** [Power]: hard white or cyan source behind/above at low angle drawing one bright line down the roof gutter, mirror housing or wing edge; body in shadow, only the contour glows, against black sky.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)
texto: - **Backlit smoke** [Pressure/Establish]: hard cyan or mercury-white punching *through* tire smoke from behind; volumetric shafts, the car a dark mass dissolving into glowing haze, red tail-light bleed inside the smoke for the danger accent. Front-lit smoke is dead gray nothing — always rim it from behind.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)
texto: - **Brake-disc glow** [Detail/Impact]: macro on the wheel, glowing orange-red rotor through the spokes as the *only* warm element (toxic heat), rim the caliper and spokes with that glow, everything else steel blue — the one ember in a cold frame.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)
texto: - **Specular on wet asphalt — the mirror** [Establish/Shift]: low bumper-height, lane stretching away, practicals (Tree, sodium lamps, headlights) reflected as long vertical smears down the wet surface as the composition's spine; pull the real lamps half out of frame, keep the mirror. Wet asphalt at night = `dramaturgy.md` §9 guilt/threat, and the cheapest way to put more cold light in frame without lifting blacks.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)
texto: - **Silhouette / contre-jour** [Power/Pressure]: helmet/shoulder as pure black shape against a blown headlight or the Tree's amber bank, one thin rim defining the form plus one glint on the visor edge, no features. The brain fills the dark with something worse than any face.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)
texto: - **The Christmas Tree as the scene's lamp and clock** [Pressure→Impact]: put the Tree bank in frame as the dominant practical — its glow the only key. Stage 1: two blue bulbs as cold points in the lacquer. Stage 2: three ambers blazing, amber-as-toxin spill on wet asphalt, held. Stage 3: green pops, a single green reflection streaks the hood. Match-cut the round bulb → round headlight → round tach.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 7. Light & color for speed without faces › Concrete lighting recipes (drop-in for the format-C Light column: source · direction · quality · what it rims)
texto: **Texture and atmosphere.** Name the grain, never "clean": fine-to-medium film grain (heaviest in shadow), halation/bloom on hard practicals (soft glow ring + hard hot core), one anamorphic flare off the dominant source, slight chromatic fringe on the hottest edges (anti-sterile test in `animatic-keyframes.md` §7). One atmospheric pressure per panel (`dramaturgy.md` §9, Kurosawa) — backlit tire smoke, frozen launch grit lit on its leading edge, heat-haze warping the rimmed edge, wet asphalt as the mirror. Don't stack smoke + haze + spray in one still or it turns to mud. Keep Tony Scott's restlessness and grain; discard his warm grade.

Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 8. Sound & rhythm
texto: ## 8. Sound & rhythm

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 8. Sound & rhythm
texto: You storyboard the **sound first**; the keyframes hang off it. The general law — **loudness in the audio = panel count** — and the descending duration staircase are the density ladder in `animatic-keyframes.md` §3, sitting on the `dramaturgy.md` §12 rhythm staircase. Do not re-derive them. The race-specific rhythm rules:

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 8. Sound & rhythm
texto: - **Engine as metronome.** Tie panel *duration* to RPM: idle = ~2s panels, redline = panels collapsing 2s → 1s → 0.5s → 8fr → 4fr toward the green. The board should read as an accelerating tachometer on mute. Annotate each panel with its on-screen life.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 8. Sound & rhythm
texto: - **Amber collapse.** The Sportsman stagger (§5) is the audible drum-roll: idle drops out on the ambers, each amber a tighter panel, the green detonates.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 8. Sound & rhythm
texto: - **The wrinkle is the one time-expansion.** Dedicate 2–3 sequential panels to the slick folding (clean → wrinkled → gripping), marked "RAMP — hold", sound dropped (the Goodyear move) — the only place time *expands* inside the loud section.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 8. Sound & rhythm
texto: - **Pull-to-intimate at the peak.** At the contest's tensest point, cut from a wide loud pass to an ECU of glove-on-shifter / breath-fog, shallow focus, void around it — engines stripped to breath only. The *quiet* panel goes *tight*; the loud panel goes wide.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 8. Sound & rhythm
texto: - **Machine talks (the governing anchor).** Strip music; the `Sound` cell reads "engine + tire only" (Audi Quattro 1984).

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 8. Sound & rhythm
texto: - **Sound leads picture by 2–3fr** (J-cuts). Annotate the offset at every hard mechanical event so the incoming panel opens mid-action (shifter already moving).

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 8. Sound & rhythm
texto: Every panel inherits a `Sound` cell even though it is a still (`dramaturgy.md` §11) — prompt the *physical consequence* of the sound (deformation, particulate, smear, heat-haze, isolation-in-void), never a named sound. Fill it.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 8. Sound & rhythm

Function tags from `role-modes.md` §4. This is the structural skeleton; for a fully worked, panel-by-panel deliverable board of this exact structure (format C, ~13 rows), use `animatic-keyframes.md` §8 — do not draw a second worked board here.

Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: ## 10. Anti-fake guard

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: The race-specific list of panels that kill credibility — do not draw. (The general per-panel earns-its-place checklist is `animatic-keyframes.md` §9; run that on every panel as well.)

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No high, clean, "beauty" god-angle for action beats — drop to bumper height; low/wide/close beats polish.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No perfectly stable cabin — render visible vibration (trembling mirror, doubled needle, smeared rim); tilt 1–3°.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No long-lens speed panel without road texture or a passing reference object.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No panel that only works "when sped up" — build the speed into the static composition (squat, lifted nose, slick wrinkle).

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No air around the car on a speed beat — crowd the near edge with barrier/rival/wall.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No sharp wheel rim on a moving car — smear the spokes into a disc.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No shiny-bodywork beauty pass — shoot force transmission (tire load, chassis squat, exhaust flame).

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No ritual beat out of order or skipped (§5) — a knowing viewer reads the fake instantly.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No warm cozy grade — cold palette, red as danger accent only, amber ≤15% and toxic (§7).

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: - [ ] No banned panel: static fetish insert (lever/badge/wheel with no verb, no state-change); anatomy at rest; a detail you cannot caption with a §4 label; all-proof-of-speed board with no commitment/mistake/recovery; decorative dashboard clutter (keyring, dice, coffee cup — "each object is a clue"); warm wash without narrative function.

encabezado: Race, speed and faceless kinetic montage › 10. Anti-fake guard
texto: Before sending the board, run `animatic-keyframes.md` §9 (per-panel master checklist), `dramaturgy.md` §15 and `universal-rules.md` §13 over it. The most-violated step is the three-detail check — do not skip it.

texto: Use one dominant director reference per scene. Translate into concrete camera, light, rhythm, blocking. Never stack three or more references.

encabezado: Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references
texto: - Fincher. Precise motivated camera. No handheld drift. Cold palette.

encabezado: Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references
texto: - Kurosawa. Weather as emotional pressure. Rain, wind, heat.

encabezado: Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references
texto: - Spielberg. Readable staging. Clear geography. Emotional wide shots.

encabezado: Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references
texto: - Edgar Wright. Sound-driven montage. Match cuts on sound events.

encabezado: Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references
texto: - Jonathan Glazer. Music-video visual idea translated to drama.

encabezado: Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references
texto: - Wong Kar-wai. Longing. Reflections. Slow emotional drift.

encabezado: Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references
texto: - Safdie. Anxiety. Handheld pressure. Overlapping sound.

encabezado: Role modes › 1. Director mode › Style references
texto: - Wes Anderson. Symmetry. Controlled blocking. Color blocks.

encabezado: Role modes › 3. Editor mode › Rules
texto: - Sound-driven transitions.

Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy
texto: ## 4. Shot function taxonomy

encabezado: Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy
texto: Every beat should carry at least one function tag. This is the editor's grammar.

encabezado: Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy
texto: - **Establish.** Where we are. Wide or master shot. Sets geography.

encabezado: Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy
texto: - **Reveal.** What appears. New information enters frame.

encabezado: Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy
texto: - **Power.** Who controls the scene right now. Staging reveals the hierarchy before dialogue does.

encabezado: Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy
texto: - **Pressure.** Tension builds. Movement toward threat or decision. Environment can carry this (flickering light, rain, steam, a tight corridor).

encabezado: Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy
texto: - **Detail.** Important object, hand, eye, texture, gesture. Macro or close-up. The anchor object often lives here.

encabezado: Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy
texto: - **Reaction.** Emotional consequence. Face response to a beat.

encabezado: Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy
texto: - **Shift.** Inner change. Body language turning point. The moment before the decision becomes visible.

encabezado: Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy
texto: - **Impact.** Decisive visual event. The drop. The hit. The break.

encabezado: Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy
texto: - **Aftermath.** Emotional residue. Stillness after impact.

encabezado: Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy
texto: - **Exit.** Final state. The image the viewer leaves with.

encabezado: Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy
texto: A full scene usually moves. Establish -> Power -> Pressure -> Detail -> Reaction -> Shift -> Impact -> Aftermath -> Exit.

encabezado: Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy
texto: A montage sequence can compress or loop. Use function tags to keep the structure readable even at high speed.

encabezado: Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy
texto: Each tag is also a question the shot must answer. Establish. Where. Power. Who commands. Pressure. What pushes. Detail. What to notice. Reaction. What it cost. Shift. What changed inside. Impact. The moment. Aftermath. The residue. Exit. The image carried out.

encabezado: Role modes › 4. Shot function taxonomy

texto: ## 1. What 2.5 changes

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 1. What 2.5 changes
texto: - **30-second native single-pass clip.** One generation, one continuous arc, no stitching. Extension pushes it to 60s; a separate Ultra Long mode goes to 180s (see sections 13-14).

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 1. What 2.5 changes
texto: - **50 multimodal references** (30 images + 10 videos + 10 audio) with per-asset role binding. The model understands which asset is responsible for character, scene, prop, camera move, or rhythm — if you tell it.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 1. What 2.5 changes
texto: - **Realistic humans are a headline feature**, not a liability: real skin pores, restrained micro-acting, multilingual lip-sync in 11 languages. The 2.0-era face caution does not apply.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 1. What 2.5 changes
texto: - **Negative commands became reliable.** "Pure video, no subtitles, no background music" now actually suppresses random subtitles and unwanted score — the classic 1.x/2.0 failure is fixed.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 1. What 2.5 changes
texto: - **Second-level timestamp control.** `[0-4s] ...` beat windows are honored as timing, not just ordering.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 1. What 2.5 changes
texto: - **Editing an existing video** (partial re-render, background swap, language re-dub) and **extending** it are first-class modes, not workarounds.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 1. What 2.5 changes
texto: - **Blockout control**: white-model 3D previz video (or green-screen plates) locks camera path, staging and blocking; Blender/Maya plugins upload straight to Jimeng.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 1. What 2.5 changes
texto: Entry points: Jimeng (jimeng.jianying.com — Omni Reference / Smart Edit / Long Video / First & Last Frames), Doubao (Pro subscription), Xiaoyunque (xyq.jianying.com — character library, 3D director stage, segment reshoot).

texto: ## 3. Official prompt formula

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 3. Official prompt formula
texto: Base formula for any 2.5 prompt:

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 3. Official prompt formula
texto:
```text
<Subject> performs <primary action or event> in <scene and environment>.
The visuals feature <visual style>.
Use <shot size, camera angle, camera movement, or cuts>.
Audio includes <dialogue, ambience, sound effects, or music>.
```

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 3. Official prompt formula
texto: Any component may be omitted. For long or reference-heavy work, the macro-formula:

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 3. Official prompt formula
texto:
```text
Complete prompt = [reference declaration] + [one-line summary] + [plot by timeline] + [global tail]
```

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 3. Official prompt formula
texto: - **Reference declaration.** Each asset by upload order + its role (character / voice / motion / scene). See section 5.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 3. Official prompt formula
texto: - **One-line summary.** Subject + place + event + genre/style + special camera treatment.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 3. Official prompt formula
texto: - **Plot by timeline.** Per beat: ➕ positive content (picture + camera + action + dialogue + SFX) and ➖ local bans ("no subtitles", "no BGM").

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 3. Official prompt formula
texto: - **Global tail.** Re-state the must-hold globals (camera position, environment, sound, lighting) and repeat the global bans.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 3. Official prompt formula
texto: Re-@ the same asset multiple times through the prompt — the official guide says repeated mentions increase accuracy.

texto: ## 5. Reference discipline (the 50-slot system)

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 5. Reference discipline (the 50-slot system)
texto: The point of 50 slots is not dumping assets in. **Every material's role must be written in the prompt.** Do not rely on text labels inside images; do not make the model infer mappings.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 5. Reference discipline (the 50-slot system)
texto: Role template:

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 5. Reference discipline (the 50-slot system)
Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 5. Reference discipline (the 50-slot system)
texto: Rules:

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 5. Reference discipline (the 50-slot system)
texto: - **Bind each subject individually.** `<Character A> corresponds to @Image 1. Use only the appearance, hairstyle, and clothing.` The officially forbidden pattern: "@Images 1 through 4 define four characters respectively" — it never states which is which.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 5. Reference discipline (the 50-slot system)
texto: - **Add exclusions** for anything that could bleed in: "Do not use the image background." / "Do not use the people in the image." / "Do not use the person's identity, clothing, or scene from the video."

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 5. Reference discipline (the 50-slot system)
texto: - **Do not restate what a reference already defines.** If a reference video defines the motion, state only which attributes to inherit — re-describing every action conflicts with the reference.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 5. Reference discipline (the 50-slot system)
texto: - **Subject Profile** for a recurring character:

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 5. Reference discipline (the 50-slot system)
texto:
```text
[Subject Profile: Conservator]
Appearance and clothing: @Image 1.
Fixed prop: <Sample Case> from @Image 5.
Locations: <Conservation Lab> and <Gallery>.
Motion references: the case-opening motion from @Video 1.
Do not use: other characters' clothing. Do not give this character <Record Board>.
```

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 5. Reference discipline (the 50-slot system)
texto: - **Select references per scene**, not all at once: `Scene 1 | Use: <list>. Event: ... End state: ...`

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 5. Reference discipline (the 50-slot system)
texto: - The same character in two states (before / after a transformation) = **two separate image slots**, each bound to its time range. Expect this to be the flakiest binding — budget re-rolls.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 5. Reference discipline (the 50-slot system)

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 6. The 30-second structure: stages and end states
texto: ## 6. The 30-second structure: stages and end states

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 6. The 30-second structure: stages and end states
texto: Divide the clip into consecutive stages. **One primary state change per stage, and always state the visible end state** — the end state is what the model steers toward (this is the U11 final-image rule, per stage).

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 6. The 30-second structure: stages and end states
texto:
```text
[Generation Goal] Generate a <video type>. The central subject is <subject>,
and the primary event is <story summary>.
[Stage 1] Initial state: ... Primary event: <one primary action>. End state: <visible state>.
[Stage 2] Continue from the previous stage: <what must remain unchanged>.
          Primary event: ... End state: ...
[Stage 3] Primary event: <closing event>. End state: <final visible state>.
[Maintain Consistency] Keep <identity, count, clothing, prop ownership,
spatial direction, audio relationships> consistent.
```

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 6. The 30-second structure: stages and end states
texto: Timestamp rules:

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 6. The 30-second structure: stages and end states
texto: - A time range is an event's **time budget, not an edit point**. Ranges must be consecutive and non-overlapping.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 6. The 30-second structure: stages and end states
texto: - **Windows of 3 seconds or more.** Shorter windows execute unreliably.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 6. The 30-second structure: stages and end states
texto: - **One core action + one camera move per window.** Do not demand frequencies ("three actions in one second").

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 6. The 30-second structure: stages and end states
texto: - Second-precision only where it matters: critical handoffs, entrances, transitions, beat hits. `At 5 seconds, the camera whip-pans left and completes the transition.` Relative triggers work too: `Three seconds after the character presses the button, the room lights turn off.`

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 6. The 30-second structure: stages and end states
texto: - Too little content in a window = model freedom; too much = over-cutting and omissions. Match content volume to the budget.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 7. The anti-collapse skeleton (3 modules)
texto: ## 7. The anti-collapse skeleton (3 modules)

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 7. The anti-collapse skeleton (3 modules)
texto: The official structure for dramatic 30-second work. It maps onto our 11-block skeleton but is leaner:

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 7. The anti-collapse skeleton (3 modules)
texto:
```text
<One-line tone summary — the logline>

[Module 1 — Reference layer]
Strictly keep @Image 1's face and features consistent. Keep @Image 2's
composition / blockout / spatial relations. Strictly lock character blocking.

[Module 2 — Global settings ("worldview + anti-collapse")]
Base environment & texture (emphasize extreme, realistic physical texture).
Visual style (film look, depth of field, lighting).
Camera language.
Character styling (use the section 8 formula).
Performance core (the acting register for the whole piece).
Prohibitions: <sound bans> + <subtitle bans> + <behavior bans> + <known collapse points>.

[Module 3 — Timestamped storyboard]
[start-end s] [beat name] — physical directives (shot size, composition,
micro-actions) + emotional subtext.
```

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 7. The anti-collapse skeleton (3 modules)
texto: Two techniques carry this skeleton:

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 7. The anti-collapse skeleton (3 modules)
texto: - **The prohibition list is specific, not generic.** From the official farewell example: "No exaggerated crying, no fast cuts, no large body movements, no extra dialogue, no BGM, no runny nose, no premature dropping of tears." Ban the exact ways this scene can collapse.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 7. The anti-collapse skeleton (3 modules)
texto: - **Directive + subtext.** After the physical directive, explain to the model *why* the action happens: "Emotion analysis: she is not complaining — she is waiting for him to confirm an answer she already guessed." The model acts better when it knows the intent. This is the official guide's signature trick and it composes directly with our Details Law.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 8. Realistic human formula (anti-AI-face)
texto: ## 8. Realistic human formula (anti-AI-face)

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 8. Realistic human formula (anti-AI-face)
texto:
```text
Character = [age / ethnicity] + [skin tone / skin texture] + [3-4 facial details]
          + [gaze / soul] + [hairstyle / hair color] + [clothing / fabric]
          + [build / emotion / aura]
```

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 8. Realistic human formula (anti-AI-face)
texto: - **Force-append the fidelity suffix:** "retaining real fine pores and skin texture" (optionally freckles, blemishes). This single clause is the official anti-plastic-skin fix.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 8. Realistic human formula (anti-AI-face)
texto: - Facial details need 3-4 concrete points: eye shape, brow bone, nose bridge, lips, jawline.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 8. Realistic human formula (anti-AI-face)
texto: - Gaze/soul = the emotion the eyes carry, separate from the facial geometry.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 8. Realistic human formula (anti-AI-face)
texto: - Works for animated characters too — swap the texture register.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 8. Realistic human formula (anti-AI-face)
texto: For one emotional transition, **2-4 observable cues are enough** (eye movement, brow tension, mouth, breathing, throat swallow, hands). More reads as overacting; abstract emotion words leave too much room.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 9. Camera language
texto: ## 9. Camera language

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 9. Camera language
texto: Officially understood without translation: extreme wide / wide / medium / close-up / extreme close-up; push in, pull out, pan, lateral move, follow shot, orbit, dive, dolly out, tilt, handheld shake; low angle, overhead, first-person; one-take shot, dolly zoom, aerial, FPV, bullet time, bounce speed ramp.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 9. Camera language
texto: For rarer terms, keep the term **and** translate it to observable change: `term + target subject + visual change + foreground/background relationship + direction or speed`. Full pattern and vocabulary in `camera-lighting-vocabulary.md` §10.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 9. Camera language
texto: Aperture and focal-length numbers are allowed, but the visible result phrased in words is what actually steers the model.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 10. Transitions
texto: ## 10. Transitions

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 10. Transitions
texto: The transition vocabulary (natural cut, fade, dissolve, flash, wipe, occlusion mask, match cut, action/whip cut, motion-relay, zoom-through, ink-wash) lives in `camera-lighting-vocabulary.md` §11. Seedance-specific usage:

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 10. Transitions
texto:
```text
cut = [transition type] + [basic constraints] + [cut logic]
```

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 10. Transitions
texto: - Always attach the incantation: **"prohibit rigid cutting, prohibit objects appearing out of thin air"** — it is the official anti-jump-cut clause, repeated in every transition template.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 10. Transitions
texto: - Transitions can be **delegated**: "From [natural cut / occlusion mask / ink-wash / match cut], choose the one that best fits the style of this film."

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 10. Transitions
texto: - Order-gate effects that must not fire early: "The ink-wash effect must only appear AFTER 25 seconds, triggered by the 'click' sound — absolutely no premature appearance."

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 11. Physics through consequences and triggers
texto: ## 11. Physics through consequences and triggers

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 11. Physics through consequences and triggers
texto: 2.5 renders real physics and couples it with audio. Exploit this in four moves:

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 11. Physics through consequences and triggers
texto: 1. **Declare the physics regime up front.** "Rain reflections on metal, water splashed by tires, and the specular refraction of exhaust flames must strictly obey real-world physics."

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 11. Physics through consequences and triggers
texto: 2. **Narrate consequences, not just actions.** Tires kick up water curtains; the impact shatters the bridge into a spider-web pattern; the shockwave blows the rain away in a ring. Action chains where each step forces the next ("hand grips jar → lid actually unscrews") double as QA — a broken chain exposes a failed generation instantly.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 11. Physics through consequences and triggers
texto: 3. **Negatively constrain the known failure.** "No soft-body or mollusk-like twisting of the mecha structure (must maintain metallic rigidity)." "The amber stays attached to the palm and must not clip through the fingers."

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 11. Physics through consequences and triggers
texto: 4. **Gate events on triggers.** "Three seconds after she presses the button..." / "only when he says {now}..." — triggers beat raw seconds for anything tied to performance.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 12. Video editing (partial re-render)
texto: ## 12. Video editing (partial re-render)

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 12. Video editing (partial re-render)
texto: 2.5 edits an existing video: replace a subject, swap a background, remove a watermark, change the spoken language — while everything else stays put. The canonical pattern:

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 12. Video editing (partial re-render)
texto:
```text
[Edit Goal] Edit @Video 1. Within <entire video or time range>,
<add / remove / replace / adjust> <object, region, or audio category>.
[Source Video Role] @Video 1 is the sole editing master. It defines <characters,
scene, actions, composition, camera movement, occlusion, audio, and event order>.
[Target Material Role] @Image 1 defines <attributes of the replacement>.
[Edit Scope] Modify only <object, region, time range, or audio category>.
[Content to Preserve] Keep <everything that must not change> from @Video 1.
```

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 12. Video editing (partial re-render)
texto: - **Subject replacement** adds a `[Timeline Inheritance]` block: "<Target> inherits every appearance, motion, occlusion, and exit of <original>, including timing, duration, path, and speed changes." Close with the catch-all: "Except for the object explicitly modified above, keep all other people, props, scene content, camera movements, cuts, and event order from @Video 1 unchanged."

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 12. Video editing (partial re-render)
texto: - **The preservation-clause opener.** For filmed footage, enumerate everything to keep before stating any change — down to focal length, aspect and floor perspective: "Fully preserve from @Video 1 the person's identity, face, hair, skin tone, lip movement, original voice, speech rhythm, expression, gestures, camera position, focal length, aspect ratio, wall and floor perspective, and total duration." The longer the keep-list, the less drift.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 12. Video editing (partial re-render)
texto: - **Anchor timing to speech, not seconds**, when the source has narration: "When they say {now look at my hand}, a golden amber appears in the palm." The voice is the timeline.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 12. Video editing (partial re-render)
texto: - **Slice long sources first.** Editing works best on clips ≤20s; longer sources stall or fail.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 12. Video editing (partial re-render)
texto: - **Audio-only edits** work: "Remove only the original background music. Keep the dialogue, lip sync, ambience, and action sound effects; preserve the visuals and editing rhythm."

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 12. Video editing (partial re-render)
texto: - **Localization pattern** — shoot once, re-dub per market: "Replace the Chinese narration in @Video 1 with natural fluent Spanish, and replace the presenter with a Spanish woman. Keep the original camera movement, blocking, performance pacing, scene, and product; preserve the overall audio-visual rhythm."

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 12. Video editing (partial re-render)
texto: - Background swap scope: "modify only the background outside the subject's silhouette."

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 13. Video extension
texto: ## 13. Video extension

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 13. Video extension
texto: Any clip ≤30s extends by 4-30s per pass, nested repeatedly, **hard ceiling 60s**. The new prompt applies only to the appended segment; original frames are untouched. Required verbs: extend forward / extend backward / continue.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 13. Video extension
texto: Forward:

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 13. Video extension
texto:
```text
Extend @Video 1 forward. The first frame of the extended segment directly
continues from the last frame of @Video 1. Maintain continuity in <pose,
prop position, background, camera position, lighting, motion direction>.
Then, <new content>.
Keep each subject as the same continuous instance throughout: do not duplicate
or split it, and keep the person's appearance stable.
```

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 13. Video extension
texto: Backward (prepend a beginning): describe the preceding events, then define @Video 1's **first frame as the extension's explicit end state**. Gotcha: materials that belong to the source video only must be flagged — "<X> must not appear early in the backward extension" — or later characters leak into the past.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 13. Video extension
texto: - Boundary frames connect visually, not pixel-identically.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 13. Video extension
texto: - Extensions hold character look, art style **and voice timbre** even without re-supplied references — plot-only extension prompts work.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 13. Video extension
texto: - Community-proven minimal extension prompt: "Extend the video. Keep character identity, facial structure, body proportions, lighting, art style, and the space fully unchanged. Only change camera movement; do not redesign character or action."

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 14. Ultra Long mode (30-180s)
texto: ## 14. Ultra Long mode (30-180s)

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 14. Ultra Long mode (30-180s)
texto: A separate mode (not the same as extension): one submission, 30-180 seconds. Restate duration and aspect ratio at the top of the prompt. Two working registers:

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 14. Ultra Long mode (30-180s)
texto: - **Timestamped** (1-minute ambient pieces): windowed beats with per-window bans — "0-20s (quiet opening): fixed camera... no shake, no characters enter, hard cuts prohibited."

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 14. Ultra Long mode (30-180s)
texto: - **Narrative flow** (3-minute pieces): loose event chain with inline references — the official 3-minute example is a cat-waiter vlog listing a full day of beats with 12 image refs assigned by role, closed with "No subtitles throughout, no background music."

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 14. Ultra Long mode (30-180s)
texto: Plan pacing in advance — without timestamps or a beat chain the back half drifts. Under the hood the pipeline generates segment-by-segment, carrying the **last ~3 seconds of each segment as the reference for the next** — which is why hand-offs are smooth and why a weak middle segment propagates forward. On Xiaoyunque the same mechanism powers chained extension to 90s plus **segment reshoot**: select a bad span on the timeline and regenerate only it, everything outside stays identical — the cheapest fix for pop-in objects and missed expressions.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 15. Blockout and green screen
texto: ## 15. Blockout and green screen

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 15. Blockout and green screen
texto: The controllability king: lock space, camera and staging in 3D first, let the model render materials and light. Two granularities:

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 15. Blockout and green screen
texto: - **Coarse blockout** — primitive geometry as a "dynamic skeleton" (trajectories, blocking, camera path, cuts, light changes). **Map every primitive to a reference**: "The tall cylinder in @Video 1 corresponds to <Guide>. The rectangular block corresponds to <Display Cart>." Exclude the render style: "Do not use its gray geometry or empty scene." Best practice: **no limbed or winged models in coarse blockouts** — unless you write the full limb motion sequence, they go stiff.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 15. Blockout and green screen
texto: - **Fine blockout** — complete 3D animation; the model re-renders materials, color and style only: "@Video 1 is a fine blockout reference. Preserve structure, action, spatial layout, camera position, camera movement, and cuts. Do not use its original gray materials or empty background. Re-render <subject> as <final subject>..." **Clean the viewport capture first**: remove path lines, coordinate axes, controllers and camera frustums. Coarse currently works better than fine.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 15. Blockout and green screen
texto: Pipeline notes:

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 15. Blockout and green screen
texto: - Blender/Maya plugins ("Clay Renderer" / 白模渲染上传器) render the blockout and upload straight to Jimeng as the reference video. Blender ≥3.6 works; no C4D/3ds Max. Color-coding blockout objects is unreliable — disambiguate primitives via prompt text, not material colors.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 15. Blockout and green screen
texto: - No 3D package? Xiaoyunque's 3D director stage reconstructs a blockout from a concept image, offers action/camera/prop libraries, and lets you **drag-draw the camera path in the viewport**, then renders the previz clip for you.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 15. Blockout and green screen
texto: - A **camera-path diagram works as an image reference** too: supply a top-down route sketch as @Image N and write "follow the camera route in @Image N".

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 15. Blockout and green screen
texto: - **Green screen, both directions**: upload green-screen footage + scene refs ("composite the person naturally into the classroom from @Image 2"), or convert an existing video's background *into* green screen for downstream comps ("Change all the white backgrounds into green screen backgrounds. Remove the sound, keep it muted.").

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 16. Storyboard grids and keyframes
texto: ## 16. Storyboard grids and keyframes

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 16. Storyboard grids and keyframes
texto: - **Storyboard grid as input**: one image, ≤15 panels official (practitioners have pushed 50), clean line art, minimal text. Declare the reading order and exclude the style: "@Image 1 provides a 12-panel storyboard grid for shot order and approximate composition. Read it left to right, top to bottom. Do not use the grid's line-art style, text labels, or placeholder characters." Then `Shot 1: ... Shot N: ...`

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 16. Storyboard grids and keyframes
texto: - **Multi-keyframe sequences**: "Use @Image 1 through @Image N as keyframes in this order", one key state per image. Independent images align better than a grid. Keyframes control stage order and key states, not exact frames.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 16. Storyboard grids and keyframes
texto: - **First + last frame** works inside omni-reference mode — declare each anchor separately ("@Image 1 is the first frame... @Image 2 is the last frame..."), never jointly. Same aspect ratio required.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 16. Storyboard grids and keyframes
texto: - This is where the `image` skill chains in: character sheets and keyframes from `animatic-keyframes.md` become the reference kit.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 17. Failure modes and fixes
texto: ## 17. Failure modes and fixes

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 17. Failure modes and fixes › Twins / face-blending in multi-person scenes
texto: ### Twins / face-blending in multi-person scenes

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 17. Failure modes and fixes › Twins / face-blending in multi-person scenes
texto: Fix. Per-subject binding (section 5) + explicit differentiation: "Their movements are not synchronized. Clothing colors, hairstyles, and facial features must all be distinct. No identical clones in the background."

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 17. Failure modes and fixes › Same character in two states appears at the wrong time
texto: ### Same character in two states appears at the wrong time

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 17. Failure modes and fixes › Same character in two states appears at the wrong time
texto: Pre/post-transformation slots confuse the model. Fix. Bind each state to its time range explicitly; budget re-rolls — this is the flakiest binding in 2.5.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 17. Failure modes and fixes › Random subtitles or unwanted BGM
texto: ### Random subtitles or unwanted BGM

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 17. Failure modes and fixes › Random subtitles or unwanted BGM
texto: Fix. "Pure video, no subtitles, no background music" — reliable in 2.5. Repeat in the global tail.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 17. Failure modes and fixes › Plastic AI skin
texto: ### Plastic AI skin

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 17. Failure modes and fixes › Plastic AI skin
texto: Fix. "Retaining real fine pores and skin texture" + production language instead of "hyperrealistic 8k".

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 17. Failure modes and fixes › Long-context plausibility slips
texto: ### Long-context plausibility slips

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 17. Failure modes and fixes › Long-context plausibility slips
texto: Over 30s the model can place a plausible object in an impossible spot (a freighter on dry concrete). Fix. State the world's hard constraints in the global tail; verify the full timeline before shipping — errors hide in the back half.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 17. Failure modes and fixes › The one-take that refuses to stay one take
texto: ### The one-take that refuses to stay one take

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 17. Failure modes and fixes › The one-take that refuses to stay one take
texto: 2.5 errs by commission: it completes more instructions than rivals but may cut freely even when told "one continuous take". Fix. "One continuous shot, no cuts of any kind" + a camera path that never motivates a cut; if montage keeps leaking in, drop to a 10-15s window where one-takes are stable.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 17. Failure modes and fixes › Edit mode stalls or ignores the instruction
texto: ### Edit mode stalls or ignores the instruction

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 17. Failure modes and fixes › Edit mode stalls or ignores the instruction
texto: Fix. Source ≤20s (slice first); name @Video 1 as "the sole editing master"; one edit target per pass.

texto: ## 18. Economics and model choice

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 18. Economics and model choice
texto: - Costs are real: a 30s/720p generation on Jimeng runs ~500-700 credits. Production budgets must assume re-rolls, extensions and segment reshoots — fix with edit/extend/reshoot instead of full regeneration whenever possible. Draft at 480p, finish at 720p.

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 18. Economics and model choice
texto: - Versus Minimax H3 (the other frontier model of this launch window): **H3 errs by omission, Seedance 2.5 errs by commission** — H3 delivers a more filmic whole but drops shots from the list; 2.5 executes nearly every instruction but may misuse a reference or break a global constraint. Pick 2.5 for timestamp precision, dense shot choreography, 50-reference kits and the editing/blockout toolchain; pick H3 (or Kling/Veo) when overall cinematic coherence per credit matters more than instruction compliance.

texto: The flagship official example for emotional performance. Abridged; the structure is what to copy:

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 19. Worked examples (official, verbatim) › A. Restrained micro-acting — "Riverside Farewell" (29s one-shot)
texto:
```text
29-Second One-Shot (Ancient Costume Woman's Riverside Farewell)

[Global Scene Setting] Early morning by the river, a blurred small boat in the
background, a lonely farewell. Quiet, restrained. Cinematic, shallow depth of
field, soft natural light. The camera holds a close-up of the woman, imitating
the subjective POV of "him" standing opposite her. Subtle handheld breathing,
one continuous shot with no fast cuts.

[Character Styling] [Age/Ethnicity] 22-year-old East Asian woman, classical
gentle cinematic face. [Skin] Cool-toned fair skin, delicate and moist,
retaining realistic fine pores and natural skin texture. [Facial Features]
Slender elegant eyes (slightly moist), relaxed brows, delicate straight nose
bridge, full lips with a faint gentle smile, soft jawline. [Eyes/Soul] Deeply
affectionate gaze, eyes shimmering like spring water. [Hair] Jet-black hair in
a casual classical low bun, a plain jade hairpin. [Clothing] Minimalist pure
white cross-collar Hanfu. [Physique/Aura] Slender, delicate narrow shoulders,
gentle classical romantic aura.

[Core Performance] Restrained and nuanced. Capture the shifting gaze, the rise
and fall of breathing, slight lip trembling, subtle brow movements, nostril
changes, throat swallowing, and the natural process of a tear sliding down.

[Negative Prompts] No exaggerated crying, no fast cuts, no large body
movements, no extra dialogue, no BGM, no runny nose, no premature dropping
of tears.

[Emotion and Action Storyboard]
Stage 1: 0-3s [Questioning]. She looks directly into the lens, lips slightly
parted, and whispers: {Are you really leaving?} Emotion analysis: she is not
complaining — she is waiting for him to confirm an answer she already guessed.
Stage 2: 3-10s [Resignation] — swallowing the bitterness. ...
Stage 3: 11-17s [Remembering] — a 0.5-second dead-silent pause; her lips twitch
then press together, jaw tightens, throat swallows.
Stage 4: 18-23s [Regret] — she lowers her eyes, and only then do the tears
begin to fall. She shakes her head slightly, almost imperceptibly.
Stage 5: 24-29s [Letting Go] — extreme close-up. She forms a gentle smile and
says in a barely audible but steadied voice: {You can go.} (On the word "go"
there is a faint tremble, forcefully suppressed.)
```

encabezado: Seedance 2.5 — production reference (ByteDance, official guides of 2026-07-31) › 19. Worked examples (official, verbatim) › B. Physics and prohibitions — sci-fi mecha chase (30s one-shot)
texto:
```text
30-Second One-Shot (Sci-Fi Mecha Chase and Transformation)

[Global Setting] A cyberpunk cross-sea bridge in 2077, heavy rain. Emphasize
extreme, realistic physical textures: rain reflections on metal, water
splashed by tires, and the specular refraction of exhaust flames must strictly
obey real-world physics. Hardcore sci-fi cinematic feel, high-contrast neon
(cyber-pink and icy blue), high-speed shutter. High-speed drone POV, one
continuous shot. Subject: a silver-and-black concept mecha motorcycle.

[Negative Prompts] No soft-body or mollusk-like twisting/clipping of the mecha
structure during movement (must maintain metallic rigidity); no human
entities; strictly remove irrelevant subtitles; force mute / no default BGM;
avoid copyrighted IP elements like Transformers or Tron.

[Timestamp Storyboard]
[00:00-00:08] [Extreme Speed] The camera skims the waterlogged road; the
spinning wide tires kick up massive water curtains meters high. Camera
subtext: convey speed through the physical interaction of rain, puddle
reflections and engine flames.
[00:09-00:16] [Evasion] The tires grind the road, sparking orange friction
sparks, executing a tight "S" curve.
[00:17-00:24] [Mid-Air Reassembly] During slow-mo hang time the armor flips,
deconstructs, and reassembles — strictly rejecting "noodle-like" soft-body
transformation.
[00:25-00:30] [Heavy Landing] The tonnage impact shatters the bridge surface
into a spider-web pattern; the shockwave blows the surrounding rain away in
an expanding ring. A frozen "superhero landing" as the final image.
```

Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 1. What Seedance is
texto: ## 1. What Seedance is

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 1. What Seedance is
texto: A ByteDance video model with the UNIQUE ability to generate several distinct shots in ONE generation. The only major model that can pack a mini-montage inside a single 5-10s clip. Good cinematic motion, strong at ads and short narrative.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 2. Versions and specs
texto: ## 2. Versions and specs

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 2. Versions and specs
texto: - Seedance 1.0 Pro. 1080p, 5-10s (API up to 12s). Strong multi-shot.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 2. Versions and specs
texto: - Seedance 1.0 Lite. 720p, faster, cheaper.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 2. Versions and specs
texto: - Seedance 1.5 Pro. Native audio and lip-sync added.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 2. Versions and specs
texto: - Seedance 2.0. Improved motion, better audio, 9 camera movement presets, limited negative prompt support, up to 12 reference inputs via `@` tags. Since June 2026: native 4K, 10-bit color. 2.0 Mini: ~2× faster, ~30% cheaper, for drafts and batches.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 2. Versions and specs
texto: - **Seedance 2.5** (released 2026-07-31). Native 30-second single-pass clip, up to 60s via extension, 30-180s in Ultra Long mode. 50 multimodal reference inputs (30 images + 10 video + 10 audio), video editing (partial re-render), 3D white-model camera blockout, realistic humans with multilingual lip-sync in 11 languages. **Full production reference: `seedance-25.md`.**

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 2. Versions and specs
texto:
Resolutions. 480p, 720p, 1080p; 2.0 adds native 4K; 2.5 outputs 480p/720p on Jimeng.
Aspect ratios. 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 9:16, 21:9, 9:21.
Frame rate. 24-30 fps.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 2. Versions and specs
texto: **Model pick within the family:** one continuous 15-30s arc, heavy reference kits, editing/extension of existing footage → 2.5 (realistic humans and lip-sync are a 2.5 headline feature — the 2.0-era face caution below does not apply to it). People-centric drama on a 2.0-only pipeline → 1.5 Pro (2.0 aggressively filters human faces and celebrity-adjacent content after the 2026 deepfake crackdown). Scenes, architecture, product, montage in short clips → 2.0. Cheap drafts → 2.0 Mini, then re-render keepers high.
