encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 4. The Details Law (read this first)
texto: ## 4. The Details Law (read this first)

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 4. The Details Law (read this first)
texto: > **Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.**

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 4. The Details Law (read this first)
texto: Seedance does not render abstractions. It renders **physical specifics**. Every adjective must be a sensory fact. Every emotion must be a body. Every shot must own at least three concrete details:

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 4. The Details Law (read this first)
texto: 1. **One environmental pressure.** Cold blue refrigerator light. Steam off boiling water. Wet asphalt. Flickering fluorescent. Dripping tap. Curtain breathing in the AC.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 4. The Details Law (read this first)
texto: 2. **One physical micro-action.** Jaw locks. Finger taps the counter. Knuckles whiten on the fork. Lips press into a line. He swallows hard.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 4. The Details Law (read this first)
texto: 3. **One sound anchor or visual motif.** Stomach growl at 2.3s. Reflection in the dark phone screen. Rain hitting the same windowpane.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 4. The Details Law (read this first)
texto: If a shot has none of these — it is filler. Delete it or rewrite it.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 4. The Details Law (read this first)
texto: Banned, lazy phrasing that produces mush:

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 4. The Details Law (read this first)
texto: - "cinematic, professional, high quality, masterpiece"

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 4. The Details Law (read this first)
texto: - "beautiful lighting"

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 4. The Details Law (read this first)
texto: - "epic scene"

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 4. The Details Law (read this first)
texto: - "amazing visuals"

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 4. The Details Law (read this first)
texto: - "he is sad / he is angry" (with no physical translation)

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 4. The Details Law (read this first)
texto: This rule is hard. Multi-shot prompts on Seedance fail not because of the model, but because the writer was lazy on a single shot. One thin shot drags the whole sequence down.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 5. Six-step prompt formula (quick scenes)
texto: ## 5. Six-step prompt formula (quick scenes)

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 5. Six-step prompt formula (quick scenes)
texto: For single-shot 5s clips with one clear action.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 5. Six-step prompt formula (quick scenes)
texto:
```text
Subject. [Who or what]
Motion. [Present-tense verb, one clear action]
Camera. [Movement + framing + lens]
Environment. [Where, props, atmosphere]
Lighting. [Direction + quality + color]
Style. [Realism level, genre reference]
```

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 5. Six-step prompt formula (quick scenes)
texto: Write in full sentences, not tags. Seedance prefers clear grammatical prose. For dramatic / multi-shot / character-locked work, **use the production-grade skeleton in section 6 instead.**

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 6. Production-grade skeleton (11 blocks)
texto: ## 6. Production-grade skeleton (11 blocks)

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 6. Production-grade skeleton (11 blocks)
texto: Use this for any dramatic piece, multi-shot ad, music-video segment, or character-locked clip. Each block answers a specific failure mode. Skipping a block reintroduces that failure.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 6. Production-grade skeleton (11 blocks)
texto:
```text
[1] Character lock.
    Use @img1 as the main character reference and preserve the exact same person
    across the whole clip: <face shape, eye color, hair, facial hair, build, distinctive
    features>. Dress him in <exact wardrobe>. No nudity. No glasses (unless reference).
    No extra characters.

[2] Length + genre + editing intent.
    Generate a <duration>-second multi-shot <genre> sequence with <fast / slow / staircase>
    dynamic editing.

[3] Story (one paragraph).
    <Concrete physical events of this clip in present tense. What changes from start to
    end. Name the break point.>

[4] Visual style.
    <Palette, contrast, grain, color temperature, what to avoid (e.g. "no warm yellow
    tones"). Texture cues — realistic skin, food detail, fabric, surfaces.>

[5] Camera style.
    <Camera body / look (e.g. Sony FX3 handheld). Lenses with purpose:
    35mm / 50mm for medium, 85mm for emotional close-ups, 100mm macro for inserts,
    24mm for wide silhouettes. Handheld micro-shake or static. Strict cuts between
    shots. No continuous take.>

[6] Editing style.
    <Hard cuts vs match cuts. Rhythmic escalation. Where the pause lands. Where the
    impact hits. The rhythmic staircase: long → shorter → shorter → pause → impact.>

[7] Audio.
    <Diegetic sounds in order: ambient, micro-actions, impact, silence moment, final
    cue. Examples: stomach growl, refrigerator hum, fork clink, wet thud, abrupt
    silence, distant city ambience. No dialogue / No subtitles / No on-screen text.>

[8] Shot-by-shot timeline.
    Shot 1, 0.0–X.X sec: <framing, lens, camera move, action, environment detail,
                           emotion translated into body>.
    Shot 2, X.X–Y.Y sec: <...>.
    ...
    (See section 7 for the 5-second rhythm template.)

[9] Lighting (recap and specifics).
    <Main source, fill, rim. Direction. Color temperature. What it carries
    psychologically — judgment, isolation, hope, grief.>

[10] Composition.
    <Where the subject sits in frame across shots. Negative space. Reflections.
    Silhouettes. Foreground obstruction. The final image must be named.>

[11] Output specs.
    <Exact duration. Aspect ratio. Realism level. CLI: --resolution 1080p
    --duration 5 --camerafixed false>
```

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 6. Production-grade skeleton (11 blocks)
texto: Why 11 blocks and not 6? Each block prevents one specific Seedance failure: identity drift, one-take collapse, mood smear, lens chaos, audio mismatch, drift on rhythm. Cheap insurance.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 7. The 5-second shot timeline (rhythm template)
texto: ## 7. The 5-second shot timeline (rhythm template)

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 7. The 5-second shot timeline (rhythm template)
texto: For a 5-second multi-shot clip, the model performs best with **5 shot beats** following a dramatic micro-arc. Use this timing as the default scaffold:

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 7. The 5-second shot timeline (rhythm template)
texto:
```text
0.0–0.8 sec  | Establish     | extreme close-up or insert that anchors emotion / situation
0.8–1.6 sec  | Action        | medium shot, hero moves or reacts
1.6–2.5 sec  | Turn          | new framing reveals the shift (POV, OTS, rack focus)
2.5–3.6 sec  | Reaction      | tight close-up, slow push-in, emotion lands on the body
3.6–5.0 sec  | Climax / hero | hero shot, low angle, slow-mo if earned, final image
```

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 7. The 5-second shot timeline (rhythm template)
texto: For 10s clips, double the structure or insert one pause before the climax (the pause beats speed). For 15s+ stories, split into 3 × 5s clips and stitch in the editor — Seedance is more reliable in shorter generations than one long take.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 8. Multi-shot syntax (unique)
texto: ## 8. Multi-shot syntax (unique)

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 8. Multi-shot syntax (unique)
texto: Seedance reads explicit cut markers inside a single prompt and generates distinct shots connected by visible cuts. This is its strongest card. Use it when you need montage in a single generation.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 8. Multi-shot syntax (unique)
texto: Supported cut markers.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 8. Multi-shot syntax (unique)
texto:
```text
Shot 1. [description]
Cut to. [description]
Camera cut to. [description]
Camera switching. [description]
Lens switch to. [description]
```

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 8. Multi-shot syntax (unique)
texto: Inline timeline syntax.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 8. Multi-shot syntax (unique)
texto:
```text
[Shot A description] -> Cut to -> [Shot B description] -> Camera cut to -> [Shot C description]
```

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 8. Multi-shot syntax (unique)
texto: Example.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 8. Multi-shot syntax (unique)
texto:
```text
Shot 1. Medium close-up on a tired man in a kitchen. He opens the refrigerator.
Cut to. Macro insert. His hand reaches toward a single sausage on an empty shelf.
Cut to. Over-the-shoulder shot. The fridge light paints his face cold blue.
```

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 8. Multi-shot syntax (unique)
texto: Use 2-3 shots per 5-second clip for tight cinematic montage, 4-5 shot beats only when each beat is short and physically distinct (see section 7). Hard cap: 5 shots per generation — beyond that the model drops or compresses shots. Size the duration to the shot count (4 shots need 10-15s, not 5s). Every shot must share an anchor with its neighbors — same character, same location, or same lighting recipe — or the model produces disconnected clips instead of a sequence.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 9. Anti-mush guard block
texto: ## 9. Anti-mush guard block

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 9. Anti-mush guard block
texto: Seedance sometimes ignores cuts and produces one continuous take, smears multiple shots into a single moving frame, or drifts character identity across the timeline. Drop this block at the **very top of the prompt** (before block [1]) when it happens or to prevent it pre-emptively on heavy multi-shot work:

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 9. Anti-mush guard block
texto:
```text
Important direction:
This must be a clearly edited multi-shot sequence with visible cuts between shots.
Do not generate a single continuous take. Each shot must have a different camera angle
and different framing. Use rapid montage pacing with rhythmic escalation. Keep the same
character appearance throughout. Preserve the same clothing, face, body type, facial
hair, and hairstyle in every shot. The tone is <serious cinematic drama / tragicomedy /
documentary realism / etc.>.
```

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 9. Anti-mush guard block
texto: This is the highest-leverage paragraph in any Seedance prompt. Add it any time the model produced mush on a previous attempt.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 10. `@img1` character reference syntax
texto: ## 10. `@img1` character reference syntax

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 10. `@img1` character reference syntax
texto: Seedance 2.0 accepts image references inline using `@img1`, `@img2`, etc. Use this to lock the protagonist's likeness across all shots in a multi-shot clip and across multiple stitched clips.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 10. `@img1` character reference syntax
texto:
```text
Use @img1 as the main character reference and preserve the exact same man across the
whole clip: <full identity block: face, eyes, hair, facial hair, build, distinctive
features, wardrobe>. No nudity. No glasses (unless in reference). No extra characters.
```

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 10. `@img1` character reference syntax
texto: Rules.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 10. `@img1` character reference syntax
texto: - The full identity block must follow the `@img1` mention. The model needs the textual description as a backup signal — the image alone drifts.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 10. `@img1` character reference syntax
texto: - Repeat the identity block in **every** clip of a stitched sequence. Treat each generation as briefing a new intern.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 10. `@img1` character reference syntax
texto: - For multiple references (character + setting, character + outfit), label each: `@img1` is the protagonist, `@img2` is the location reference, `@img3` is the outfit reference. Then state the role inline.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 10. `@img1` character reference syntax
texto: - 2.0 also takes `@Video1` (motion/style reference, 480-720p) and `@Audio1` (voiceover / music) tags — state each reference's role in prose, e.g. "@Audio1 plays as the voiceover". Limits: 12 files total on 2.0 (up to 9 images, 3 videos, 3 audio); up to 50 on 2.5.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 11. Camera movements (9 presets)
texto: ## 11. Camera movements (9 presets)

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 11. Camera movements (9 presets)
texto: - Dolly Out. Reveals context, pulling away.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 11. Camera movements (9 presets)
texto: - Dolly In. Pushes into subject, builds tension.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 11. Camera movements (9 presets)
texto: - Pan Left / Pan Right. Horizontal reveal, landscape, row.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 11. Camera movements (9 presets)
texto: - Tilt Up / Tilt Down. Vertical reveal.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 11. Camera movements (9 presets)
texto: - Tracking. Follows a moving subject.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 11. Camera movements (9 presets)
texto: - Crane / Aerial. Epic scale, establishing.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 11. Camera movements (9 presets)
texto: - Handheld. Documentary, intimate, UGC.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 11. Camera movements (9 presets)
texto: - Zoom In / Zoom Out. Tension or detail.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 11. Camera movements (9 presets)
texto: - Hitchcock Zoom. "dolly out while zooming in" for vertigo effect.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 11. Camera movements (9 presets)
texto: - Static (via `--camerafixed true`). Locked frame.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 11. Camera movements (9 presets)
texto: Combine sparingly. Multiple camera moves in 5s rarely resolve cleanly.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 12. Negative prompts
texto: ## 12. Negative prompts

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 12. Negative prompts
texto: Seedance 1.0 Pro does NOT support negative prompts. No `--no blur` syntax works.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 12. Negative prompts
texto: Seedance 2.0 adds limited negative prompt support but it's fragile and often ignored.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 12. Negative prompts
texto: Workaround for 1.x/2.0. Always invert to positive phrasing. Instead of "no yellow tones" write "cold blue-gray palette with desaturated skin tones." Instead of "no distorted hands" write "anatomically correct hands with clear finger separation."

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 12. Negative prompts
texto: **Seedance 2.5 fixed this.** Direct bans are reliable: "pure video, no subtitles, no background music" actually suppresses them, and specific prohibition lists ("no exaggerated crying, no fast cuts") are a core part of the official 2.5 prompt structure. See `seedance-25.md` §7.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 13. Image-to-video rule
texto: ## 13. Image-to-video rule

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 13. Image-to-video rule
texto: When using a reference image, DO NOT describe elements already visible in the image. The model sees it. Describe only motion and camera work. Re-describing static elements creates identity drift.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 13. Image-to-video rule
texto:
Bad. "A man in red shirt stands in kitchen. He walks to the fridge."
Good. "He slowly walks toward the fridge, opens it with hesitation, freezes when he sees the empty shelves. Tracking shot from behind, 35mm."

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 14. Audio (1.5+)
Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 14. Audio (1.5+)
texto: Seedance 1.5 Pro, 2.0 and 2.5 generate native audio and support lip-sync. Include audio cues in the body of the prompt — treat the prompt as a sound brief.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 14. Audio (1.5+)
texto:
```text
Audio. fridge hum, distant rain on window, one stomach growl at 2.3 sec, final silence.
```

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 14. Audio (1.5+)
texto: Rules:

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 14. Audio (1.5+)
texto: - Dialogue goes in **double quotes** on 1.5/2.0 — the model voices it, generates the voice and syncs lips to the cut. State the delivery: "Play her line dry and a little proud, his quiet and worn out." **On 2.5, use the dedicated markers instead**: dialogue in `{ }`, SFX in `< >`, music in `( )`, titles in `【 】` (see `seedance-25.md` §4).

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 14. Audio (1.5+)
texto: - Keep lines short. Long monologues drift out of sync — split into several lines and hold sync with cuts. Still less robust than Veo for speech-first work.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 14. Audio (1.5+)
texto: - Write **"no music"** explicitly when you want none — otherwise the model lays an ad-style score under everything.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 14. Audio (1.5+)
texto: - Subtitles: describe the voiceover, then ask for "text along the bottom edge, timed to the voice".

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes
texto: ## 15. Failure modes and fixes

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes › One continuous take when multi-shot was requested
texto: ### One continuous take when multi-shot was requested

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes › One continuous take when multi-shot was requested
texto: Fix. Add explicit "Cut to" markers. Say "multi-shot sequence with visible hard cuts. Do not generate a single continuous take."

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes › Character drift across shots
texto: ### Character drift across shots

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes › Character drift across shots
texto: Fix. Repeat the full identity block at each shot boundary inside the prompt.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes › Motion ignored below 5 seconds
texto: ### Motion ignored below 5 seconds

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes › Motion ignored below 5 seconds
texto: Fix. Minimum duration 5s for any scene that has multiple actions or camera moves.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes › Negative phrasing ignored
texto: ### Negative phrasing ignored

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes › Negative phrasing ignored
texto: Fix. Use positive substitutes. Seedance 1.0 has no negative parser.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes › Multi-shot fails on 4+ shots in 5s
texto: ### Multi-shot fails on 4+ shots in 5s

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes › Multi-shot fails on 4+ shots in 5s
texto: Fix. Cap at 2-3 shots per 5-second clip for tight cinematic, or 4-5 short beats following the section 7 timeline. If more shots are needed, split into multiple generations.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes › Mood smear / "everything looks the same"
texto: ### Mood smear / "everything looks the same"

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes › Mood smear / "everything looks the same"
texto: Fix. Each shot needs a distinct emotional function (Establish / Power / Pressure / Detail / Reaction / Shift / Impact / Aftermath — see dramaturgy.md §10, Layer 2). If two adjacent shots have the same function, the model averages them into the same frame. Vary function and framing in every cut.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes › Lazy abstract phrasing produces lifeless clips
texto: ### Lazy abstract phrasing produces lifeless clips

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes › Lazy abstract phrasing produces lifeless clips
texto: Fix. Apply the Details Law (section 4). Audit your draft: every shot must have one environmental pressure, one micro-action, one sound or visual motif anchor. Replace adjectives like "dramatic", "intense", "beautiful" with concrete physical facts.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes › Human faces rejected or degraded (2.0)
texto: ### Human faces rejected or degraded (2.0)

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 15. Failure modes and fixes › Human faces rejected or degraded (2.0)
texto: After the 2026 deepfake crackdown, 2.0 aggressively filters human faces, helmets, sunglasses, and anything resembling protected IP or celebrity likeness. Fix. Route face-heavy drama to Seedance 2.5 (realistic humans are its headline feature), 1.5 Pro, Kling, or Veo; keep 2.0 for scenes, architecture, product and montage work. Use only owned or synthetic character references — the IP/celebrity filter applies on 2.5 too.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 16. Worked example. 15-second tragicomedy as 3 × 5s clips
texto: ## 16. Worked example. 15-second tragicomedy as 3 × 5s clips

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 16. Worked example. 15-second tragicomedy as 3 × 5s clips
texto: A 15s narrative is **never** one prompt. It is three self-contained 5-second prompts, each with the full character lock, the full visual style, the full audio block, and a different dramatic function. Stitch in the editor.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 16. Worked example. 15-second tragicomedy as 3 × 5s clips › Story spine
texto: ### Story spine

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 16. Worked example. 15-second tragicomedy as 3 × 5s clips › Story spine
texto: - Beat 1 (Clip A, 0-5s). Hunger. Hero opens an almost empty fridge. Discovers one lonely sausage. Despair flips to hope.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 16. Worked example. 15-second tragicomedy as 3 × 5s clips › Story spine
texto: - Beat 2 (Clip B, 5-10s). Cooking. Pot, water, fire, sausage, bubbling, anticipation, hero shot lifting the sausage with a fork.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 16. Worked example. 15-second tragicomedy as 3 × 5s clips › Story spine
texto: - Beat 3 (Clip C, 10-15s). Catastrophe. Sausage slips, falls, wet thud. Window. Bedroom. Hungry sleep. Cut to black.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 16. Worked example. 15-second tragicomedy as 3 × 5s clips › Clip A. Hunger (production-grade skeleton applied)
texto: ### Clip A. Hunger (production-grade skeleton applied)

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 16. Worked example. 15-second tragicomedy as 3 × 5s clips › Clip A. Hunger (production-grade skeleton applied)
texto:
```text
Important direction:
This must be a clearly edited multi-shot sequence with visible cuts between shots.
Do not generate a single continuous take. Each shot must have a different camera angle
and different framing. Use rapid montage pacing.

Use @img1 as the main character reference and preserve the exact same man across the
whole clip: bald head, gray-green eyes, round expressive face, moustache, long black
braided goatee, short dark side hair tufts, slightly overweight build, tragicomic face.
Dress him in a dark oversized T-shirt and dark sweatpants. No nudity. No glasses.
No extra characters.

Generate a 5-second multi-shot tragicomic cinematic sequence with fast dynamic editing.

Story:
The man is hungry at night. He suddenly goes to the refrigerator, opens it, feels
disappointment because it is almost empty, then notices one lonely sausage and becomes
instantly hopeful.

Visual style:
Cold night kitchen. Blue-green refrigerator light. Desaturated colors. No warm yellow
tones. Slightly harsh LED reflections. Realistic cinematic look. High contrast but
natural skin texture. Subtle film grain. Realistic food detail.

Camera style:
Sony FX3 handheld look. 35mm and 50mm lenses for medium and close shots. 100mm macro
for inserts. Handheld micro-shake. Visible cuts between shots.

Editing style:
Fast montage with hard cuts. Each shot a different angle and framing. Tense rhythm,
escalating to the moment of discovery.

Audio:
Deep stomach growl, soft room tone, refrigerator hum, quiet footsteps, fridge door
sound. No dialogue. No subtitles. No on-screen text.

Shot 1, 0.0–0.8 sec. Extreme close-up of the man's eyes in darkness. He is awake,
hungry, tense. Static close shot, faint blue ambient light.
Shot 2, 0.8–1.6 sec. Medium handheld side shot. He sits up and walks fast to the
kitchen. Slight shake, push-in.
Shot 3, 1.6–2.6 sec. POV from inside the refrigerator. The door opens toward camera.
Cold blue-green light hits his face. Shelves almost empty. His face drops.
Shot 4, 2.6–3.5 sec. Rapid inserts: empty shelf, empty container, lonely sauce stain,
his sad eyes, his hand moving items aside.
Shot 5, 3.5–5.0 sec. Macro insert of one single sausage in the corner. Rack focus
from empty shelf to sausage. Smash cut to a slightly low-angle close-up of his face.
His eyes widen, despair flips to joy, tiny victorious smile.

Lighting:
Dark apartment, very low ambient fill. Main source is cold refrigerator light,
blue-green, top-front. Strong contrast. No warm kitchen light.

Composition:
Tight close-ups and inserts. Negative space inside the empty fridge. Final face shot
heroic and absurd.

--resolution 1080p --duration 5 --camerafixed false
```

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 16. Worked example. 15-second tragicomedy as 3 × 5s clips › Clip A. Hunger (production-grade skeleton applied)
texto: Clips B and C follow the same structure with their own story paragraph, shot list, and final image. The character lock and visual style blocks are repeated **verbatim** in each clip — Seedance has no memory between generations.

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 16. Worked example. 15-second tragicomedy as 3 × 5s clips › Older single-clip skeleton (kept for quick scenes)

encabezado: Seedance reference (ByteDance) › 16. Worked example. 15-second tragicomedy as 3 × 5s clips › Older single-clip skeleton (kept for quick scenes)

texto: # Universal rules — apply to every video model

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model
texto: These rules apply to Seedance, Kling, Veo, and any other AI video generator. They exist because all current video models share a common failure mode. They reward concrete physical direction. They punish abstraction, contradictions, and keyword spam. Ignoring these produces muddy generations regardless of which model you target.

Universal rules — apply to every video model › 1. The non-negotiable. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.
texto: ## 1. The non-negotiable. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 1. The non-negotiable. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.
texto: This is the most violated rule in AI video, and the one reason most multi-shot prompts fail. The dramaturgy is fine — the writer just got lazy on a single shot, and that one thin shot drags the whole sequence into mush.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 1. The non-negotiable. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.
texto: Every shot in every prompt owns at least three concrete physical details:

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 1. The non-negotiable. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.
texto: 1. **One environmental pressure.** Cold blue refrigerator light. Steam off boiling water. Wet asphalt. Flickering fluorescent. Dripping tap. Curtain breathing in the AC. (Kurosawa: weather is a character. See `dramaturgy.md` §9.)

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 1. The non-negotiable. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.
texto: 2. **One physical micro-action.** Jaw locks. Knuckles whiten on the fork. Lips press into a line. He swallows hard. Fingers curl against the doorframe. (Show, not tell — the body is the only place where feelings render.)

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 1. The non-negotiable. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.
texto: 3. **One sound anchor or visual motif.** Stomach growl at 2.3s. Reflection in a darkened phone screen. Rain on the same windowpane. A single fluorescent flicker before each cut.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 1. The non-negotiable. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.
texto: If a shot has none of these — it is filler. Delete it or rewrite it. No exceptions for "establishing", "transition", or "hero product" shots — those are exactly the shots that go lazy first.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 1. The non-negotiable. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.
texto: Words that do not render and mark the writer being lazy:

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 1. The non-negotiable. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.
texto: - "cinematic", "professional", "high quality", "masterpiece", "stunning", "epic", "amazing"

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 1. The non-negotiable. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.
texto: - "beautiful lighting", "dynamic camera", "intense moment", "powerful scene"

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 1. The non-negotiable. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.
texto: - "he is sad", "she is angry", "he is afraid" — emotions named without a body

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 1. The non-negotiable. Details intensify emotion. Laziness kills the prompt.
texto: Replace each with concrete physical facts. The full theory of why this works lives in `dramaturgy.md` §2 (Second law).

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 2. U1. Universal prompt skeleton
texto: ## 2. U1. Universal prompt skeleton

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 2. U1. Universal prompt skeleton
texto: Build every prompt from these layers, roughly in this order:

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 2. U1. Universal prompt skeleton
texto:
```text
[Subject / Character]
[Action / Motion]
[Scene / Environment]
[Camera / Shot / Lens]
[Lighting / Atmosphere]
[Style / Mood / Palette]
[Sound / Audio]
[Duration / Aspect ratio / Resolution]
[Continuity rules]
[Negative constraints — only if the model supports them]
```

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 2. U1. Universal prompt skeleton
texto: Model-specific skeletons live in their reference files (`seedance.md`, `kling.md`, `veo.md`). For dramatic / multi-shot / character-locked Seedance work, the production-grade 11-block skeleton in `seedance.md` §6 supersedes this generic skeleton.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 3. U2. Weight-at-start
texto: ## 3. U2. Weight-at-start

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 3. U2. Weight-at-start
texto: Generators put more attention on the first 30-40% of tokens. Lead with subject and action. Style modifiers go at the end. Camera, lighting, and environment live in the middle.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 4. U3. Show don't tell
texto: ## 4. U3. Show don't tell

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 4. U3. Show don't tell
texto: The model cannot render feelings. It renders bodies. Translate every emotion into a physical action.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 4. U3. Show don't tell
texto: - Bad. "He is scared."

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 4. U3. Show don't tell
texto: - Good. "His jaw locks. He stops breathing for one beat. His fingers curl against the doorframe."

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 4. U3. Show don't tell
texto: Calibration: for one emotional transition, **2-4 observable cues** (eye movement, brow tension, mouth, breathing, throat swallow, hands) are enough. Fewer leaves the model guessing; more reads as overacting.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 5. U4. Natural language beats tag spam
texto: ## 5. U4. Natural language beats tag spam

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 5. U4. Natural language beats tag spam
texto: Video models are not image models. Tag stuffing like "masterpiece, 4k, cinematic, beautiful" fails. Write in full cinematic sentences as if briefing a human DOP.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 6. U5. One primary camera move per shot
texto: ## 6. U5. One primary camera move per shot

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 6. U5. One primary camera move per shot
texto: Do not stack three camera moves in a 5-second clip. Pick one dominant move (dolly-in, pan, tracking, static). Layer a subtle micro-adjustment if needed (slight handheld shake, gentle rack focus). More than that produces visual chaos.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 7. U6. Precise lens language
texto: ## 7. U6. Precise lens language

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 7. U6. Precise lens language
texto: State the lens. "Shot on 50mm" works across all major models. Quick map:

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 7. U6. Precise lens language
texto: - 24mm. wide, immersive, exaggerated space

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 7. U6. Precise lens language
texto: - 35mm. natural documentary

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 7. U6. Precise lens language
texto: - 50mm. intimate, human perspective

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 7. U6. Precise lens language
texto: - 85mm. portrait, compressed background

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 7. U6. Precise lens language
texto: - 100mm macro. texture, detail

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 7. U6. Precise lens language
texto: - anamorphic 40mm. cinematic widescreen

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 7. U6. Precise lens language
texto: Full vocabulary in `camera-lighting-vocabulary.md`.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 8. U7. Character consistency anchor
texto: ## 8. U7. Character consistency anchor

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 8. U7. Character consistency anchor
texto: Anchor identity at the START of every prompt. In a multi-clip sequence, repeat the full identity block in every single prompt. Video generators have no memory between generations. Treat every clip like briefing a brilliant intern with memory damage.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 8. U7. Character consistency anchor
texto: Identity block must include: face shape, eye color, skin tone. Hair color, length, style. Facial hair. Exact clothing items. Distinctive accessories.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 8. U7. Character consistency anchor
texto: Model-specific syntax for character locking:

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 8. U7. Character consistency anchor
texto: - Seedance: `@img1` reference + identity block (see `seedance.md` §10)

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 8. U7. Character consistency anchor
texto: - Kling 1.x – 2.x: Element Binding with 3-4 reference images (see `kling.md` §7)

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 8. U7. Character consistency anchor
texto: - Kling 3.0: in-prompt `[Character A: <full identity>]` labels, optionally combined with Element Library (see `kling.md` §3)

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 8. U7. Character consistency anchor
texto: - Veo: reference ingredients / JSON identity (see `veo.md`)

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 9. U8. No contradictions
texto: ## 9. U8. No contradictions

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 9. U8. No contradictions
texto: The model obeys the strongest signal. Contradictions produce artifacts.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 9. U8. No contradictions
texto: - Bad. "Still pond" + "flowing water."

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 9. U8. No contradictions
texto: - Bad. "Close-up" + "wide cinematic landscape."

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 9. U8. No contradictions
texto: - Bad. "Quiet moment" + "explosive action."

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 10. U9. Concrete physical detail over abstract concept
texto: ## 10. U9. Concrete physical detail over abstract concept

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 10. U9. Concrete physical detail over abstract concept
texto: "Loneliness" does not render. "A man sitting alone, shoulders collapsed, face lit by blue phone glow, empty bottles on the table" does.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 10. U9. Concrete physical detail over abstract concept
texto: This is the same rule as the Details Law in section 1, viewed from a different angle. Section 1 is the audit. This is the principle.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 10. U9. Concrete physical detail over abstract concept
texto: Corollary — **consequence prompting**. Current models render real physics, so describe the consequence of an action, not just the action: tires kick up water curtains; the hand grips the jar and the lid actually unscrews; the impact shatters the surface into a spider-web pattern. Action chains where each step forces the next also work as QA — a broken chain exposes a failed generation at a glance.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 11. U10. Duration discipline
texto: ## 11. U10. Duration discipline

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 11. U10. Duration discipline
texto: Most models work in 5-10 second clips. Longer narratives live in multiple clips stitched in the editor. Do not cram a 30-second story into a 5-second prompt.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 11. U10. Duration discipline
texto: Default splits:

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 11. U10. Duration discipline
texto: - 10s = 2 clips × 5s

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 11. U10. Duration discipline
Universal rules — apply to every video model › 11. U10. Duration discipline
Universal rules — apply to every video model › 11. U10. Duration discipline
Universal rules — apply to every video model › 11. U10. Duration discipline
texto: Three exceptions:

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 11. U10. Duration discipline
texto: - Seedance — 2-3 shots inside one 5-10s clip via "Cut to" syntax (see `seedance.md` §8).

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 11. U10. Duration discipline
texto: - Kling 3.0 — up to 6 shots inside one generation, up to 15s, with native audio and dialogue (see `kling.md` §3).

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 11. U10. Duration discipline
texto: - Seedance 2.5 — up to 30s in one pass. The working structure is consecutive stages, each with one primary state change and an explicit visible end state (see `seedance-25.md` §6).

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 12. U11. The final image rule
texto: ## 12. U11. The final image rule

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 12. U11. The final image rule
texto: Every clip needs a clear final frame. The model uses the ending as emotional destination.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 12. U11. The final image rule
texto: - "Ends on his face frozen in the blue refrigerator light" beats "he stands there sadly."

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 12. U11. The final image rule
texto: The final image is also one of the five anchors (see `dramaturgy.md` §13). Naming it is non-negotiable.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 13. U12. The three-detail check (audit before sending)
texto: ## 13. U12. The three-detail check (audit before sending)

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 13. U12. The three-detail check (audit before sending)
texto: Before returning the final prompt to the user, audit every shot. Each shot must carry at least one of each:

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 13. U12. The three-detail check (audit before sending)
texto: 1. Environmental pressure (lighting, weather, surface, sound of the room).

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 13. U12. The three-detail check (audit before sending)
texto: 2. Physical micro-action on the body (jaw, hand, breath, eye, gesture).

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 13. U12. The three-detail check (audit before sending)
texto: 3. Sound anchor or recurring visual motif tied to the emotional spine.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 13. U12. The three-detail check (audit before sending)
texto: If a shot has zero, fix it before sending. If a shot has only one, ask whether you can make it two without bloat. The strongest prompts in this skill's worked examples always have all three.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 13. U12. The three-detail check (audit before sending)
texto: Empty descriptors that fail this check: "establishing wide shot", "beautiful lighting", "dynamic camera move", "cinematic look", "intense moment", "dramatic close-up". Replace each with three concrete physical facts.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 14. U13. Reference role discipline
texto: ## 14. U13. Reference role discipline

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 14. U13. Reference role discipline
texto: Wherever a model accepts reference assets (Seedance `@Image/@Video/@Audio`, Kling Element Binding and Omni references, Veo ingredients), **every asset gets an explicit role written in the prompt**: what it defines (appearance, motion, voice, scene, camera path) and what to ignore ("Do not use the image background", "Do not use the people in the image").

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 14. U13. Reference role discipline
texto: - Bind each subject individually: "<Character A> corresponds to @Image 1 — use only the appearance, hairstyle, and clothing." Never the collective form "@Images 1 through 4 define four characters respectively" — it does not state which is which.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 14. U13. Reference role discipline
texto: - Do not restate what a reference already defines. If a video reference carries the motion, name only the attributes to inherit; re-describing every action fights the reference.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 14. U13. Reference role discipline
texto: - More assets is not more control. Control comes from role clarity; unassigned assets bleed into the frame.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 14. U13. Reference role discipline
texto: Model-specific limits and templates live in the model files (`seedance-25.md` §5 has the fullest system).

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 15. U14. Priority declaration
texto: ## 15. U14. Priority declaration

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 15. U14. Priority declaration
texto: When a prompt is overloaded (10+ scenes, many subjects, spatial tricks), adding more description makes it worse. Instead, declare priorities — the model cannot know what matters most unless told what to protect and what to sacrifice:

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 15. U14. Priority declaration
texto: 1. The core subject that must survive every shot.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 15. U14. Priority declaration
texto: 2. The key shots that must appear.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 15. U14. Priority declaration
texto: 3. The transitions where the model may freestyle.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 15. U14. Priority declaration
texto: 4. The mandatory final frame.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 15. U14. Priority declaration
texto: This ranks above prompt-length discipline: a shorter prompt with declared priorities beats a longer one without them.

encabezado: Universal rules — apply to every video model › 15. U14. Priority declaration

Veo reference (Google) › 1. What Veo is
texto: ## 1. What Veo is

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 1. What Veo is
texto: Google's cinematic video model with NATIVE synchronized audio. The only major generator that creates dialogue, SFX, and music in sync with the video and does lip-sync natively. Best for commercial polish, narrative with dialogue, and cinematic audio.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 2. Versions and specs
texto: ## 2. Versions and specs

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 2. Versions and specs
texto: - Veo 3. Text-to-video, native audio, 4 / 6 / 8 second clips.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 2. Versions and specs
texto: - Veo 3.1. Adds image-to-video with First Frame, improved audio, reference ingredients, stronger motion coherence.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 2. Versions and specs
texto:
Duration. 4, 6, or 8 seconds.
Dialogue budget. Max 8 seconds of spoken audio per clip.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 3. Prompt structure and length
texto: ## 3. Prompt structure and length

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 3. Prompt structure and length
texto: Order matters. Lead with subject and camera. Quality modifiers go at the end.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 3. Prompt structure and length
texto:
```text
[Subject / Action]
+ [Environment / Setting]
+ [Camera / Shot Type / Lens]
+ [Lighting / Atmosphere]
+ [Style / Quality]
+ [Audio]
+ [Duration]
```

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 3. Prompt structure and length
texto: Sweet spot. 50-200 words.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 3. Prompt structure and length
texto: - Shorter prompts = more creative latitude, less control.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 3. Prompt structure and length
texto: - Longer prompts = tighter control, higher risk of contradictions.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical)
texto: ## 4. Dialogue syntax (critical)

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical)
texto: Veo is the only model that renders synced lip movement and voice. The syntax matters.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical) › Required format
texto: ### Required format

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical) › Required format
texto: Double quotes + lead-in verb (says, whispers, shouts, mutters, asks).

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical) › Required format
texto:
```text
A woman says, "Welcome to the future."
He whispers, "Don't move."
She shouts, "Get out!"
```

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical) › Required format
texto: Colon after the lead-in verb works too and is often more reliable.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical) › Required format
texto:
```text
A woman says: "Welcome to the future."
```

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical) › Voice character modifiers
texto: ### Voice character modifiers

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical) › Voice character modifiers
texto: Place modifiers before the lead-in verb.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical) › Voice character modifiers
texto:
```text
He says in a weary voice, "We are fine. We are fine."
She whispers nervously, "I don't want to be here."
He shouts excitedly, "We did it!"
```

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical) › Timing rule
texto: ### Timing rule

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 4. Dialogue syntax (critical) › Timing rule
texto: Maximum 8 seconds of spoken audio. Cram too many words into a 5s clip and the delivery speeds up unnaturally. Cut the line until it fits.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 5. SFX syntax
texto: ## 5. SFX syntax

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 5. SFX syntax
texto: Three supported formats. Mix as needed.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 5. SFX syntax
texto:
```text
SFX: thunder cracks in the distance
Audio: rain on tin roof, distant traffic, one slow breath
(a loud thunderclap)
(key turning in a lock)
(wet footsteps on concrete)
```

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 5. SFX syntax
texto: Use labels `Audio:`, `Says:`, `SFX:` to separate sound direction from visual direction. The model needs an explicit signal that audio should be generated.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique)
texto: ## 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique)

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique)
texto: Veo parses structured JSON. This prevents "concept bleed" where describing mood accidentally changes object colors. Use JSON for complex scenes with strict continuity needs.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique) › Full schema
texto: ### Full schema

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique) › Full schema
Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique) › When to use JSON
texto: ### When to use JSON

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique) › When to use JSON
texto: - Multiple scenes in one generation.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique) › When to use JSON
texto: - Strict character continuity across shots.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique) › When to use JSON
texto: - Complex props that must stay the same color and size.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique) › When to use JSON
texto: - When a prose prompt kept changing subject colors when you added mood words.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 6. JSON prompts (powerful, unique) › When to use JSON
texto: Not every Veo prompt needs JSON. For simple clips, prose is faster and often better.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 7. Image-to-video (Veo 3.1)
texto: ## 7. Image-to-video (Veo 3.1)

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 7. Image-to-video (Veo 3.1)
texto: Uses the static image as First Frame. Prompt guides motion and sound.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 7. Image-to-video (Veo 3.1)
texto: Rules.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 7. Image-to-video (Veo 3.1)
texto: - Do not re-describe static elements.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 7. Image-to-video (Veo 3.1)
texto: - Describe only motion, camera, light change, and audio.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 7. Image-to-video (Veo 3.1)
texto: - Add "maintain the subject from the first frame" to protect identity.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 7. Image-to-video (Veo 3.1)
texto: Example.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 7. Image-to-video (Veo 3.1)
texto:
```text
Maintain the subject from the first frame. Slow push-in, 50mm. She exhales, her eyes shift to the left, one strand of hair falls across her forehead. Warm rim light grows stronger.

Audio: soft breath, distant traffic, one door closing in the next room.
Duration: 6 seconds.
```

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 8. Reference ingredients (3.1)
texto: ## 8. Reference ingredients (3.1)

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 8. Reference ingredients (3.1)
texto: Upload multiple reference images (character, location, prop) and tag them in the prompt.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 8. Reference ingredients (3.1)
texto:
```text
The character from reference_1 walks into the location from reference_2 holding the object from reference_3.
```

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 8. Reference ingredients (3.1)
texto: Use when you need a specific character in a specific place with a specific object.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes
texto: ## 9. Failure modes and fixes

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Dialogue speeds up unnaturally
texto: ### Dialogue speeds up unnaturally

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Dialogue speeds up unnaturally
texto: Fix. Cut the line to fit 8 seconds of natural speech. Test by reading aloud.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Audio missing from output
texto: ### Audio missing from output

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Audio missing from output
texto: Fix. Add explicit `Audio:`, `SFX:`, or `Says:` labels. Do not assume the model will infer audio from visual description.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Camera direction ignored
texto: ### Camera direction ignored

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Camera direction ignored
texto: Fix. Lead the prompt with camera. "Wide aerial shot" at the start beats "cinematic camera work" in the middle.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Character color changes when mood words are added
texto: ### Character color changes when mood words are added

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Character color changes when mood words are added
texto: Fix. Switch to JSON prompt. Lock the character description in the continuity block. Keep mood in global_style where it cannot bleed into object colors.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Lip-sync off
texto: ### Lip-sync off

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Lip-sync off
texto: Fix. Check the lead-in verb. "She says, ..." outperforms just quoted speech alone. Colon form often more reliable than comma.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Prompt too long, model cherry-picks
texto: ### Prompt too long, model cherry-picks

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 9. Failure modes and fixes › Prompt too long, model cherry-picks
texto: Fix. Compress to the 50-100 word range. Or switch to JSON which handles length better because of structural separation.

texto: ### JSON version

texto: See section 6. Copy the schema and fill in.

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 10. Skeleton › Worked example. Commercial hero shot
texto: ### Worked example. Commercial hero shot

encabezado: Veo reference (Google) › 10. Skeleton › Worked example. Commercial hero shot
texto:
```text
A woman in a cream silk blouse stands in front of a morning window, lifting a ceramic coffee cup to her lips. Medium close-up, 85mm, slow push-in. Warm window key from frame-left, soft bounce fill from frame-right. Cinematic naturalism, creamy palette, shallow depth of field.

```

---
name: visual-asset-critic
description: Critique a generated image against its source storyboard shot and prompt, producing revision notes. Use when the user has generated an image and wants feedback before committing. Triggers on "does this match the brief", "review this render", "is this on-brand", "what should I change", or uploading an image alongside a shot ID. The QA loop for AI visuals. Works even without a storyboard-architect run. Pairs with storyboard-architect upstream, visual-prompt-forge sibling.
---

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic
texto: # Visual Asset Critic

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic
texto: You are the editorial second-eye on AI-generated images. Most teams don't have one, they generate, glance, accept, and ship. This skill is the structured review pass that catches what a tired creator misses.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic
texto: The output is a critique with concrete, actionable revision notes. Not vibes. Not "looks good." Specific, prompt-level or post-level fixes.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › When to use
texto: ## When to use

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › When to use
texto: Trigger when the user:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › When to use
texto: - Uploads or links a generated image with a question about quality

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › When to use
texto: - Asks "does this match the storyboard"

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › When to use
texto: - Says "review this render", "is this on-brand", "what should I change"

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › When to use
texto: - Has a generated image and a `shots.json` shot reference and wants QA

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › When to use
texto: - Has a generated image and just wants editorial feedback (no storyboard reference)

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › What you produce
texto: ## What you produce

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › What you produce
texto: **Two artifacts from every review, always both:** a human-readable markdown critique (the primary surface) and a machine-readable critique JSON (so a pipeline can gate on the verdict instead of parsing prose). The JSON is detailed in Step 6; it never replaces the markdown.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › What you produce
texto:
The JSON goes to `output/critiques/round-{N}/{shot_id}.critique.json`. One file per shot
per round, never a shared filename. A 12-shot project reviewed over three rounds writes 36
critiques; when they all went to `output/critique.json` it kept one, and which one depended
on review order.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › What you produce
texto: The markdown critique uses these sections:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › What you produce
texto:
```
## Verdict
ACCEPT / REVISE / REJECT, one line

## What's working
2–4 specific positives. Concrete observations, not flattery.

## What's not working
2–5 specific issues. Each one cites a layer. Brand Lock, Series Lock, Shot Spec, Composition, Technical, or Continuity.

## Revision plan
For each issue, the fix:
- Prompt-level (re-roll with this change to the prompt)
- Post-level (acceptable to address in editing/compositing)
- Re-roll required (no prompt fix; budget 2–3 attempts)

## Confidence
HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW, how sure you are about the verdict
```

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
texto: ## Inputs

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
texto: You need:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
texto: | Input | Required? | Default if absent |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
texto: | The generated image | Yes | Cannot critique without it |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
texto: | Shot ID + shots.json | Recommended | If absent, ask for shot intent in a sentence |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
texto: | brand-lock.snapshot.md | Recommended | If absent, critique only on technical merits |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
texto: | The original prompt used | Helpful | If absent, infer from intent |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Inputs
texto: If only the image is provided with no context, ask for one piece of information: **what was this shot supposed to be?** A single sentence is enough to anchor the critique.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow
texto: ## Workflow

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent
texto: ### Step 1. Establish intent

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent
texto: What was this shot supposed to do? Pull from:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent
texto: - Shot's `rationale` field (if shots.json provided)

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent
texto: - Shot's `subject`, `framing`, `angle`, `motion` fields

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent
texto: - User's stated intent (if no shots.json)

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent
texto: - The beat this shot serves

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 1. Establish intent
texto: If you can't establish intent in one sentence, ask. Don't critique blind.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: ### Step 2. Critique by layer

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: Read `references/critique-rubric.md` for the full rubric. Quick version, check the image against:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: 1. **Brand Lock**, does it respect palette, mood, "never" list?

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: 2. **Series Lock**, does it match character/environment/lighting anchors?

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: 3. **Shot Spec**, does framing/angle/composition match the spec?

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: 4. **Composition**, does it reserve space for on-screen text if applicable?

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: 5. **Technical**, skin texture, hands, eyes, anatomy, AI artifacts?

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: 6. **Continuity**, if previous shots in the series are available, does it match?

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 2. Critique by layer
texto: For each layer, note: pass / soft fail / hard fail. The verdict aggregates these.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes
texto: ### Step 3. Map issues to fixes

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes
texto: For every "not working" point, the critique must say what to do about it. Three buckets:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes
texto: **Prompt-level fix**, change the prompt and re-roll. Specify the exact change:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes
texto: > "The character has brown hair instead of salt-and-pepper. Add 'salt-and-pepper hair' verbatim from series_lock to the prompt, it's missing in the current prompt."

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes
texto: **Post-level fix**, acceptable to address in compositing. Specify what:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes
texto: > "Color grade is slightly cool, push warmth +5 in post, no need to re-generate."

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes
texto: **Re-roll required**, no prompt fix will help; the generator just produced a bad sample. Budget 2–3 attempts:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 3. Map issues to fixes
texto: > "Hands are mangled. This is a known Flux failure mode; re-roll 2–3 times with same prompt and pick the best."

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 4. Verdict
texto: ### Step 4. Verdict

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 4. Verdict
texto: | Verdict | When |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 4. Verdict
Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 4. Verdict
texto: | ACCEPT | All layers pass or soft-fail in ways post can fix |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 4. Verdict
texto: | REVISE | One or two layers hard-fail; clear fix path |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 4. Verdict
texto: | REJECT | Three+ layers fail or one critical layer (Brand Lock, Series Lock) hard-fails with no clear fix |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence
texto: ### Step 5. Confidence

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence
texto: Be honest about uncertainty:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence
texto: | Confidence | When |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence
Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence
texto: | HIGH | Storyboard reference + brand-lock + prompt all available, clear assessment |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence
texto: | MEDIUM | Some references missing but core intent is clear |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence
texto: | LOW | Only the image, intent is inferred; verdict is your best guess |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 5. Confidence
texto:
HIGH is a factual claim about what you had, not a mood. `tools/validate_critique.py`
rejects a `1.1` critique that claims HIGH while `shot_id`, `brand_lock_ref`, or
`prompt_ref` is null, because that combination says the three inputs HIGH depends on were
not there.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: ### Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto:
After writing the markdown critique, **also** write
`output/critiques/round-{N}/{shot_id}.critique.json` conforming to
`templates/critique.schema.json` at version `1.1`. Same review, two surfaces. The markdown
is for the human; the JSON is so an automated QA loop (e.g. `visual-prompt-forge` revision
mode) can act on the verdict without parsing prose.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: **Map the markdown to the schema, section for section:**

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | Markdown | JSON field |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `## Verdict` | `verdict` (`ACCEPT` / `REVISE` / `REJECT`) |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `## What's working` bullets | `working[]` (one string each) |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `## What's not working` + `## Revision plan` | `issues[]`, merge them: each issue carries its layer/note from "what's not working" and its `fix_type`/`fix` from the matching revision-plan line |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `## Confidence` | `confidence` (`HIGH` / `MEDIUM` / `LOW`) |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto:
**Provenance, all of it required at 1.1.** A verdict is a claim about specific bytes. Name
them, and hash them:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | Field | Value |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `run_id`, `round` | from `run.json` and the round directory you are writing into |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `created_at` | UTC instant, `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ` |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `shot_id` | the shot, or `null` for a standalone image with no storyboard |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `image_ref`, `image_sha256` | the frame you reviewed, and its SHA-256 |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `prompt_ref`, `prompt_sha256` | the prompt file it came from, and its SHA-256 |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `brand_lock_ref`, `brand_lock_sha256` | the snapshot you judged against, and its SHA-256 |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `generator`, `model_version` | the generator id from `_capabilities.json`, and its model version |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `seed` | if the generator exposes one, else `null` |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto:
```bash
shasum -a 256 output/frames/round-1/shot_03.png \
              output/prompts/round-1/flux.txt \
              output/brand-lock.snapshot.md
```

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto:
Every one of those fields is required, and every one is nullable. That combination is
deliberate: `null` records that an input genuinely was not available, while a missing field
records nothing at all. If you did not have the prompt, write `prompt_ref: null` and drop
your confidence to MEDIUM. Do not omit the key.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto:
The hashes are the point. Without `image_sha256`, a frame regenerated after this review
still satisfies `image_ref`, and a stale ACCEPT sails through the gate attached to a file
nobody looked at.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: **Severity, assign one per issue.** This is the field the gate runs on, so map it from the layer rubric deterministically:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | Severity | Means | Maps from |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `minor` | soft-fail, fixable in post | a soft-fail on any layer; `fix_type: post-level` |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `major` | hard-fail **with** a clear fix path | a hard-fail that a prompt change or re-roll fixes |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: | `blocking` | hard-fail on a critical layer (Brand Lock / Series Lock) with **no** clear fix, or a defect that makes the asset unusable | an unrecoverable hard-fail |

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: **Gating rule, the verdict is derived from severities, not chosen freely.** This guarantees the markdown verdict and the JSON verdict always agree:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: - Any `blocking` issue ⇒ verdict is `REJECT`.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: - Three or more `major` issues ⇒ verdict is `REJECT`.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: - One or two `major` issues (and no blocking) ⇒ verdict is `REVISE`.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: - Only `minor` issues, or none ⇒ verdict is `ACCEPT` (with post notes).

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto:
The three-major rule used to read "escalate to REJECT at your discretion." Discretion in a
gate is not a gate, and it disagreed with `references/critique-rubric.md`, which called
three hard fails a REJECT outright. It is now a threshold, and the validator enforces it.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 6. Emit structured output (critique JSON)
texto: Pick the markdown `## Verdict` by this same rule.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate
texto: ### Step 7. Run the gate

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate
texto: Writing a schema-valid critique is not the same as passing the gate. Run it:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate
texto:
```bash
python tools/validate_critique.py output/critiques/round-1/shot_03.critique.json
```

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate
texto:
Or check the whole tree at once, which also recomputes every hash against the files on
disk:

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate
texto:
```bash
python tools/validate_provenance.py output/
```

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate
texto:
This step is not optional and it is not someone else's job. A critique that says `ACCEPT`
while carrying a `major` issue is a bug, and the only reason to write a validator for that
bug is to actually run it. Before this step existed, the gate ran in CI against two
fixtures that ship in the repo and never once against a real client's critique.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Workflow › Step 7. Run the gate
texto:
Worked examples: `examples/critique.accept.json` and `examples/critique.revise.json` show
the shape at version `1.0`, which is still valid and carries no provenance.
`examples/worked-run/critiques/` shows version `1.1` with real hashes, two shots across two
rounds.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules
texto: ## Hard rules

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 1. No vibes-based critique
texto: ### Rule 1. No vibes-based critique

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 1. No vibes-based critique
texto: "Looks great" / "feels off" without specifics is not a critique. Every observation must reference something in the image (composition, color, anatomy, lighting direction, etc.).

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 2. Prompt-level fixes must be specific
texto: ### Rule 2. Prompt-level fixes must be specific

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 2. Prompt-level fixes must be specific
texto: "Change the prompt" is not a fix. "Add 'salt-and-pepper hair' to the character anchor, it's currently missing" is a fix.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 3. Don't critique what wasn't asked
texto: ### Rule 3. Don't critique what wasn't asked

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 3. Don't critique what wasn't asked
texto: If the brief was "founder at laptop, calm mood" and the generation delivered exactly that, don't note that "the room could be more visually interesting." That's scope creep, not critique.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 4. Be honest about generator limits
texto: ### Rule 4. Be honest about generator limits

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 4. Be honest about generator limits
texto: Some failures (mangled hands, weird eye reflections, jewelry shimmer) are known generator weaknesses. Surface them as such, don't pretend a different prompt will fix them. Recommend re-roll or post.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 5. When in doubt, ACCEPT and recommend post
texto: ### Rule 5. When in doubt, ACCEPT and recommend post

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Hard rules › Rule 5. When in doubt, ACCEPT and recommend post
texto: Generation is one stage in a pipeline. If the image is 80% right and the gap is fixable in post, that's an ACCEPT with post notes. Don't send the user back to re-generate when an editor would handle it in 90 seconds.

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Reference
texto: ## Reference

encabezado: Visual Asset Critic › Reference
texto: - `references/critique-rubric.md`, the full layer-by-layer rubric

texto: ## Motion language

encabezado: Brand Lock: WhyStrohm › Motion language
