texto: | Eyes | Symmetrical, focused | Slight asymmetry | Wonky eyes, wrong reflections |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 5. Technical check
texto: | Skin texture | Natural | Slightly plastic | Heavy AI plastic |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 5. Technical check
texto: | Anatomy | Correct | Minor weirdness | Major anatomy errors |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 5. Technical check
texto: | Background artifacts | Clean | Minor weirdness | Distorted text, melted objects, impossible geometry |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 5. Technical check
texto: Technical hard fails are almost always **re-roll required**. The prompt was probably fine; the generator just produced a bad sample. Budget 2–3 re-rolls.

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 6. Continuity check (if previous shots available)
texto: ## Layer 6. Continuity check (if previous shots available)

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 6. Continuity check (if previous shots available)
texto: | Check | Pass | Soft fail | Hard fail |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 6. Continuity check (if previous shots available)
Critique Rubric › Layer 6. Continuity check (if previous shots available)
texto: | Character match | Same person, same look | Slight drift | Clearly different person |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 6. Continuity check (if previous shots available)
texto: | Lighting continuity | Same direction, time of day | Subtle shift | Direction reversed, time of day jumped |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 6. Continuity check (if previous shots available)
texto: | Environment continuity | Same space | Slight environment drift | Different space |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 6. Continuity check (if previous shots available)
texto: | Color grade match | Identical | Subtle shift | Visibly different |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Layer 6. Continuity check (if previous shots available)
texto: Continuity hard fails break the storyboard. REVISE with verbatim-anchor checks on the prompt.

encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity
texto: ## From pass/fail to severity

encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity
texto:
The tables above grade each check as pass, soft fail, or hard fail. The JSON critique
records a severity instead, and the verdict is derived from those severities. Map them
this way, and only this way:

encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity
texto: | Rubric result | Severity | Why |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity
Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity
texto: | Soft fail on any layer | `minor` | Post can absorb it. `fix_type` is usually `post-level` |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity
texto: | Hard fail **with** a clear fix path | `major` | A prompt change or a re-roll resolves it |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity
texto: | Hard fail on Brand Lock or Series Lock **with no** fix path | `blocking` | Nothing downstream recovers this |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › From pass/fail to severity
texto: | Any defect that makes the asset unusable | `blocking` | Same, regardless of layer |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto: ## Aggregating verdict

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto: The verdict follows from the severities. It is not a separate judgement:

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto: | Severities present | Verdict |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto: | any `blocking` | REJECT |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto: | three or more `major` | REJECT |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto: | one or two `major` | REVISE |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto: | only `minor`, or none | ACCEPT (with post notes) |

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto:
`tools/validate_critique.py` enforces exactly this table, so a critique that disagrees with
it fails rather than shipping. Earlier versions of this file counted hard fails and called
3+ a REJECT while the skill said "escalate at your discretion." Those two rules disagreed,
and the disagreement is the reason the threshold is now a number.

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Aggregating verdict
texto:
Soft fails are noted but don't change the verdict on their own. If you have three or more of
them, look again: a cluster of soft fails usually means one of them is really a hard fail
you talked yourself out of.

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember
texto: ## Speed bumps to remember

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember
texto: - **Don't critique what wasn't asked**, if the spec didn't call for cinematic mood, don't say "could be more cinematic"

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember
texto: - **Don't pile-on once verdict is set**, if you're rejecting, list the issues that drive the rejection; don't list every cosmetic concern

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember
texto: - **Be specific, always**, "lighting is off" is not a critique; "key light is camera-right but series_lock says camera-left" is

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember
texto: - **Cite the layer**, every issue gets tagged with which layer it falls under. This makes the fix path obvious

encabezado: Critique Rubric › Speed bumps to remember
texto: - **Distinguish prompt failure from generator failure**, if the prompt was fine and the generator produced garbage hands, that's "re-roll required", not "fix the prompt"
"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
"$id": "https://whystrohm.com/schemas/shotkit/critique.schema.json",
"title": "Critique",

"description": "Machine-readable verdict for one generated frame reviewed against its shot spec and brand-lock. The structured sibling of the markdown critique. Version 1.1 adds run provenance: the frame, prompt, and brand-lock are identified by content hash as well as by path, so a verdict can be proven to describe the bytes that were actually reviewed. Every provenance field is required at 1.1 and explicitly nullable, so an absent input is a recorded decision rather than an omission.",
"type": "object",
"required": ["version", "verdict", "confidence", "issues"],
"additionalProperties": false,
"properties": {
"version": {
"type": "string",

"description": "1.1 adds run_id, round, created_at, the *_sha256 hashes, prompt_ref, generator, model_version, seed, and the meta passthrough. 1.0 documents remain valid and are treated as legacy: they carry a verdict with no proof of what it reviewed."
"meta": {
"type": "object",
"description": "Forward-compat passthrough for tooling that needs to annotate a critique without a schema bump. Ignored by core skills.",
"additionalProperties": true
"run_id": {
"oneOf": [
{ "type": "null" },
"description": "The run this critique belongs to. Matches run.json:run_id. Format: UTC compact timestamp, a dash, then 8 hex characters."
"round": {
"oneOf": [
{ "type": "null" },
{ "type": "integer", "minimum": 1 }
"description": "Revision round, 1-indexed. Round 1 is the first generation pass."
"created_at": {
"oneOf": [
{ "type": "null" },
"type": "string",
"description": "UTC ISO-8601 instant the critique was written. Second precision, trailing Z required."
"shot_id": {
"oneOf": [
{ "type": "null" },
{ "type": "string", "pattern": "^shot_[0-9]{2,3}$" }
"description": "Shot this frame was generated for. Null when critiquing a standalone image with no storyboard."
"brand_lock_ref": {
"oneOf": [
{ "type": "null" },
{ "type": "string", "minLength": 1 }
"description": "Path to the brand-lock.snapshot.md the frame was judged against, relative to the output directory root. Null when no brand-lock was available, which caps confidence at MEDIUM."
"brand_lock_sha256": {
"oneOf": [
{ "type": "null" },
{ "type": "string", "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{64}$" }
"description": "SHA-256 of the brand-lock file as read. Null only when brand_lock_ref is null."
"image_ref": {
"oneOf": [
{ "type": "null" },
{ "type": "string", "minLength": 1 }
"description": "Path to the frame that was critiqued, relative to the output directory root."
"image_sha256": {
"oneOf": [
{ "type": "null" },
{ "type": "string", "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{64}$" }
"description": "SHA-256 of the frame bytes as reviewed. This is what makes the verdict falsifiable: if the file at image_ref no longer hashes to this value, the verdict does not describe it."
"prompt_ref": {
"oneOf": [
{ "type": "null" },
{ "type": "string", "minLength": 1 }
"description": "Path to the prompt file the frame was generated from, relative to the output directory root. Null when the prompt is unknown, which caps confidence at MEDIUM."
"prompt_sha256": {
"oneOf": [
{ "type": "null" },
{ "type": "string", "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{64}$" }
"description": "SHA-256 of the prompt file. Null only when prompt_ref is null."
"generator": {
"oneOf": [
{ "type": "null" },
{ "type": "string", "pattern": "^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$" }
"description": "Generator id that produced the frame. Must match an id in visual-prompt-forge/adapters/_capabilities.json. Null when unknown."
"model_version": {
"oneOf": [
{ "type": "null" },
{ "type": "string", "minLength": 1 }
"description": "Model version string as of generation, copied from the capability matrix entry. The matrix records what is current; this records what ran."
"seed": {
"oneOf": [
{ "type": "null" },
{ "type": "integer" },
{ "type": "string", "minLength": 1 }
"description": "Generation seed if the generator exposes one. Null when it does not."
"verdict": {
"type": "string",
"enum": ["ACCEPT", "REVISE", "REJECT"]
"confidence": {
"type": "string",
"enum": ["HIGH", "MEDIUM", "LOW"]
"working": {
"type": "array",
"description": "Concrete positives. Observations, not flattery.",
"items": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 }

encabezado: Tools
texto: # Tools

encabezado: Tools
texto:
Python helpers that keep the repo honest, gate a real project's output, and render previews
without invoking Claude.

encabezado: Tools › Requirements
texto: ## Requirements

encabezado: Tools › Requirements
texto:
```bash
pip install pyyaml jsonschema
```

encabezado: Tools › Requirements
texto: Standard library otherwise. No pandas, no numpy.

encabezado: Tools › Run everything
texto: ## Run everything

encabezado: Tools › Run everything
texto:
```bash
./tools/check.sh            # every check, with output
./tools/check.sh --quiet    # pass/fail lines only
PYTHON=python3.12 ./tools/check.sh
```

encabezado: Tools › Run everything
texto: This is exactly what CI runs, so a green local run means a green PR.

encabezado: Tools › Run everything
texto:
Every validator below also ships a `--selftest` that constructs failing fixtures and fails if
the check does not catch them. A validator that silently stops catching things is worse than
no validator, and the selftests are how that gets noticed.

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks
texto: ## Repo checks

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_skills.py`
texto: ### `validate_skills.py`

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_skills.py`
texto:
Checks every `SKILL.md` in `skills/` has the required YAML frontmatter, a `name` that matches
its directory and a substantive `description`.

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_skills.py`
texto:
```bash
python tools/validate_skills.py
```

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_schemas.py`
texto: ### `validate_schemas.py`

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_schemas.py`
texto:
Checks every `*.schema.json` file is itself valid JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) and carries
`$id`, `title`, and `description`.

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_schemas.py`
texto:
```bash
python tools/validate_schemas.py
```

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_schemas.py`
texto: It validates schemas, not instances. For instances, see `validate_shots.py`.

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_capabilities.py`
texto: ### `validate_capabilities.py`

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_capabilities.py`
texto:
Checks the generator capability matrix
(`skills/visual-prompt-forge/adapters/_capabilities.json`) against
`capabilities.schema.json`, then checks it against the adapter prose that defers to it:

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_capabilities.py`
texto: - every generator id has an adapter `.md` and every adapter `.md` has an entry

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_capabilities.py`
texto: - no adapter advertises more words than its own `max_prompt_words` ceiling

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_capabilities.py`
texto: - every adapter documents the `aspect_param` the matrix says to send

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_capabilities.py`
texto: - no `notes` field cites a word count above its own ceiling

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_capabilities.py`
texto: - warns when the matrix or an entry is past its 120-day freshness window

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_capabilities.py`
texto:
```bash
python tools/validate_capabilities.py
python tools/validate_capabilities.py --selftest
```

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_capabilities.py`
texto:
The prose checks exist because the matrix and the adapters had drifted in three places while
every file repeated the rule that the JSON wins.

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_brand_lock.py`
texto: ### `validate_brand_lock.py`

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_brand_lock.py`
texto:
Checks a brand-lock has all required sections and Identity fields, that its palette declares
the five roles the HTML preview maps onto CSS variables, and that its fonts are in the
backticked form the tools read.

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_brand_lock.py`
texto:
```bash
python tools/validate_brand_lock.py brand-packs/whystrohm.md
python tools/validate_brand_lock.py --require-configured brand-packs/whystrohm.md
python tools/validate_brand_lock.py --snapshot output/brand-lock.snapshot.md
python tools/validate_brand_lock.py --snapshots     # every snapshot in the repo
python tools/validate_brand_lock.py --selftest
```

encabezado: Tools › Repo checks › `validate_brand_lock.py`
texto:
A brand-pack may be an unfilled template; that is what a template is. A snapshot may not, and
`--snapshot` additionally requires the `<!-- snapshot taken: ... -->` and
`<!-- source: ... -->` header, with a full UTC instant preferred over a bare date.

encabezado: Tools › Project checks
texto: ## Project checks

encabezado: Tools › Project checks
texto: These run against a project's output directory, not the repo.

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_shots.py`
texto: ### `validate_shots.py`

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_shots.py`
texto:
Validates `shots.json` and `text-overlays.json` as instances, plus every cross-field and
cross-file rule JSON Schema cannot express: `end` after `start`, no gaps or overlaps, span
matching `project.duration_s`, overlay references resolving in both directions, every overlay
reachable from some shot, overlay timing inside its shot window, and every overlay color
present in the brand-lock palette.

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_shots.py`
texto:
```bash
python tools/validate_shots.py output/
python tools/validate_shots.py path/to/shots.json
python tools/validate_shots.py --examples     # every bundled example
python tools/validate_shots.py --selftest
```

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_shots.py`
texto:
Warnings cover the judgement calls: overlay copy repeated in a shot subject, a raw hex in a
subject, shot ids out of chronological order, a font the brand-lock does not declare.

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_prompts.py`
texto: ### `validate_prompts.py`

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_prompts.py`
texto:
Validates the prompt files `visual-prompt-forge` writes, against `shots.json` and the
capability matrix. Header completeness, generator id, aspect agreement, the
`max_prompt_words` ceiling, shot coverage, duplicate blocks, and the forge's two hard
rules: no on-screen text copy inside a prompt, and `environment` / `lighting` /
`color_grade` appearing verbatim.

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_prompts.py`
texto:
```bash
python tools/validate_prompts.py output/
python tools/validate_prompts.py output/prompts/round-1/flux.txt
python tools/validate_prompts.py --examples
python tools/validate_prompts.py --selftest
```

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_prompts.py`
texto:
The verbatim check is the reason this file exists. Series consistency depends on the
series_lock anchors landing unedited in every prompt, and that is the single easiest rule
in the kit to break, because paraphrasing an anchor is what writing good prose feels like.
A careful authoring pass over a seven-shot storyboard drifted on it seven times out of
seven with every other validator green, and so did the worked-run fixture in this repo.

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_prompts.py`
texto:
The character anchor is a warning rather than an error: a shot with no person in it can
legitimately omit it, and the message says so, so you can confirm rather than guess.

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_critique.py`
texto: ### `validate_critique.py`

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_critique.py`
texto:
Validates a critique against `critique.schema.json` **and** the two invariants the schema
cannot hold.

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_critique.py`
texto:
The gate: any `blocking` issue forces `REJECT`, three or more `major` issues force `REJECT`,
one or two `major` forbid `ACCEPT`.

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_critique.py`
texto:
The provenance rules, from schema version `1.1`: a hash without its path is not a reference,
`image_ref` may not be null, `HIGH` confidence requires the shot, brand-lock, and prompt all
to be identified, and a named generator has to exist in the capability matrix.

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_critique.py`
texto:
```bash
python tools/validate_critique.py output/critiques/round-1/shot_03.critique.json
python tools/validate_critique.py output/          # every critique in the tree
python tools/validate_critique.py --examples
python tools/validate_critique.py --selftest
```

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_critique.py`
texto:
Version `1.0` critiques still pass, with a warning: they carry a verdict and no way to tie it
to the bytes it reviewed.

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_provenance.py`
texto: ### `validate_provenance.py`

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_provenance.py`
texto:
Walks an output tree and recomputes every recorded hash. This is the tool that answers "does
this verdict still describe the file it reviewed."

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_provenance.py`
texto:
```bash
python tools/validate_provenance.py output/
python tools/validate_provenance.py output/ --require-accept
python tools/validate_provenance.py output/ --json
python tools/validate_provenance.py --selftest
```

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_provenance.py`
texto: It catches, with a selftest for each:

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_provenance.py`
texto: - a frame regenerated after its critique (`image_sha256` no longer matches)

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_provenance.py`
texto: - a brand-lock edited mid-project (`brand_lock_sha256` no longer matches `run.json`)

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_provenance.py`
texto: - a frame on disk with no critique for its round, never reviewed at all

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_provenance.py`
texto: - two critiques for the same shot in the same round, two operators colliding

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_provenance.py`
texto: - rounds that skip a number, or a critique whose `run_id` belongs to another run

encabezado: Tools › Project checks › `validate_provenance.py`
texto:
`--require-accept` makes it the pipeline stop condition: exit 0 only when the chain is intact
*and* every shot's latest verdict is ACCEPT.

encabezado: Tools › Rendering
texto: ## Rendering

encabezado: Tools › Rendering › `shots-to-html.py`
texto: ### `shots-to-html.py`

encabezado: Tools › Rendering › `shots-to-html.py`
texto: Renders an output folder into a single `preview.html`.

encabezado: Tools › Rendering › `shots-to-html.py`
texto:
```bash
python tools/shots-to-html.py output/
python tools/shots-to-html.py output/ --inline-images
python tools/shots-to-html.py output/ --out review.html
python tools/shots-to-html.py output/ --rendered-at 2026-07-30T00:00:00Z
python tools/shots-to-html.py --selftest
```

encabezado: Tools › Rendering › `shots-to-html.py`
texto:
It renders `skills/storyboard-html-preview/templates/preview.html.tpl`, the same structural
template the skill uses, through the small engine in `_template.py`. It did not always: the
CLI used to build its HTML inline while claiming to share the template, so the two could and
did diverge.

encabezado: Tools › Rendering › `shots-to-html.py`
texto:
Everything interpolated is HTML-escaped. Shot subjects and rationales are model-generated
prose, and one angle bracket used to be enough to break the page.

encabezado: Tools › Rendering › `shots-to-html.py`
texto:
`--rendered-at` pins the render timestamp, which makes output reproducible. CI re-renders
every bundled preview with a pinned value and fails if a byte moves.

encabezado: Tools › Rendering › `shots-to-html.py`
texto:
The page shows two dates, deliberately: the **run** date from `run.json`, and the **render**
date. A single "Generated" date meant re-rendering a preview restamped the run as today.

encabezado: Tools › Rendering › `copy-prompt.py`
texto: ### `copy-prompt.py`

encabezado: Tools › Rendering › `copy-prompt.py`
texto:
Pipes one shot's prompt to the clipboard so you can paste into a generator UI without hunting
through the file.

encabezado: Tools › Rendering › `copy-prompt.py`
texto:
```bash
python tools/copy-prompt.py output/prompts/round-1/flux.txt
python tools/copy-prompt.py output/prompts/round-2/revised-flux.txt --shot shot_02
python tools/copy-prompt.py output/prompts/round-1/flux.txt --list
python tools/copy-prompt.py --selftest
```

encabezado: Tools › Rendering › `copy-prompt.py`
texto:
Reads both file shapes the forge writes. Comment lines inside a shot block are annotations and
never land in the clipboard, so a revision file's `# fix [...]` notes are shown but not
copied. Revision files used to be unreadable to this tool entirely, which was awkward given
they are the files an operator pastes from most.

encabezado: Tools › Rendering › `copy-prompt.py`
texto: Pure standard library. `pbcopy` on macOS, `xclip` or `xsel` on Linux, `clip` on Windows.

encabezado: Tools › Internal modules
texto: ## Internal modules

encabezado: Tools › Internal modules
texto: Not entry points. Imported by the tools above.

encabezado: Tools › Internal modules
texto:
- `_shotkit.py`, hashing, run ids, brand-lock parsing, and the output-tree path conventions.
  One copy, so no two tools can disagree about what a palette or a frame path is.

encabezado: Tools › Internal modules
texto:
- `_template.py`, the template engine: `{{var}}`, `{{{raw}}}`, `{{#each}}`, `{{#if}}`. Only
  the subset `preview.html.tpl` uses, deliberately.

encabezado: Tools › Adding new tools
texto: ## Adding new tools

encabezado: Tools › Adding new tools
texto: - Make it executable (`chmod +x`)

encabezado: Tools › Adding new tools
texto: - Add a usage docstring at the top of the file

encabezado: Tools › Adding new tools
texto: - Give it a `--selftest` that proves the check fires

encabezado: Tools › Adding new tools
texto: - Document it in this README

encabezado: Tools › Adding new tools
texto: - Wire it into `tools/check.sh`, which is what CI calls

def make_run_id(now: datetime | None = None, nonce: str | None = None) -> str:
    """Build a run_id. Pass `now` and `nonce` to make it reproducible in tests."""
    now = (now or datetime.now(timezone.utc)).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    stamp = now.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")
    if nonce is None:
        nonce = sha256_text(now.isoformat() + str(id(now)))[:8]
    return f"{stamp}-{nonce}"

def run_id_timestamp(run_id: str) -> str | None:
    """Extract the compact timestamp from a run_id, or None if malformed."""
    m = RUN_ID_RE.match(run_id or "")
    return m.group(1) if m else None

Matches the documented format:
        **Display font:** `Inter Black 900`, headline weight, ...
        **Body font:** `Inter Medium 500`, body copy, ...
        **Mono font:** `JetBrains Mono Regular`, code, data, ...

Mono is optional. A brand-lock that declares one has three legal overlay fonts,
    not two, which is why the font check reads all three rather than assuming a pair.
    """
    out: dict[str, str | None] = {
        "display_font": None,
        "body_font": None,
        "mono_font": None,
    }
    # The value has to be backticked and sit immediately after the label. That is what
    # separates a real declaration from the template's instructional prose
    # ("**Display font:** font name, weights used (e.g. `Inter Black 900`)"), which
    # would otherwise resolve to the example font.
    for key, label in (
        ("display_font", "Display"),
        ("body_font", "Body"),
        ("mono_font", "Mono"),
    ):
        pattern = re.compile(
            r"^\*\*" + label + r"\s+font[^:*]*:?\*\*[ \t]*`([^`\n]+)`",
            re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE,
        )
        m = pattern.search(text)
        if m:
            value = m.group(1).strip()
            if value and not value.startswith("_"):
                out[key] = value
    return out

Only the subset the template actually uses is implemented, deliberately: variable
substitution, a loop, and a truthiness block. It exists so the CLI and the
storyboard-html-preview skill render the same structural template instead of two
hand-maintained copies that drift apart.

Supported syntax:
    {{name}}            HTML-escaped substitution
    {{{name}}}          raw substitution, for pre-built markup such as inlined CSS
    {{#each items}}     iterate a list of dicts; inside the block, keys resolve
    {{/each}}           against the item first, then the enclosing context
    {{#if name}}        render when the value is truthy
    {{/if}}

Unknown names render empty rather than raising, which keeps a partially populated
context from producing a traceback in front of a client.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import html
import re

BLOCK_RE = re.compile(r"\{\{#(each|if)\s+([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\s*\}\}")
RAW_VAR_RE = re.compile(r"\{\{\{\s*([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\s*\}\}\}")
VAR_RE = re.compile(r"\{\{\s*([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\s*\}\}")

def _find_block_end(text: str, kind: str, start: int) -> int:
    """Index of the closing tag matching the block opened before `start`."""
    open_re = re.compile(r"\{\{#" + kind + r"\s+[A-Za-z0-9_]+\s*\}\}")
    close_tag = "{{/" + kind + "}}"
    depth = 1
    pos = start
    while depth:
        next_close = text.find(close_tag, pos)
        if next_close == -1:
            raise ValueError(f"unclosed {{{{#{kind}}}}} block")
        next_open = open_re.search(text, pos, next_close)
        if next_open:
            depth += 1
            pos = next_open.end()
            continue
        depth -= 1
        pos = next_close + len(close_tag)
    return pos

def render(template: str, context: dict) -> str:
    """Render `template` against `context`."""
    out: list[str] = []
    pos = 0

out.append(_render_leaf(template[pos : block.start()], context))
        kind, name = block.group(1), block.group(2)
        body_start = block.end()
        block_end = _find_block_end(template, kind, body_start)
        close_len = len("{{/" + kind + "}}")
        body = template[body_start : block_end - close_len]
pos = block_end
return "".join(out)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run every shotkit check. This is what CI calls, so a green local run means a green PR.
#
# Usage:
#   ./tools/check.sh            # run everything, report a summary
#   ./tools/check.sh --quiet    # only print failures and the summary
#
# Requires: pip install pyyaml jsonschema
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." || exit 1

PYTHON="${PYTHON:-python3}"
QUIET=0
[[ "${1:-}" == "--quiet" ]] && QUIET=1

PASSED=0
FAILED=0
FAILED_NAMES=()

run() {
  local label="$1"
  shift
  local output
  if output=$("$PYTHON" "$@" 2>&1); then
    PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))
    if [[ "$QUIET" == "0" ]]; then
      echo "PASS  ${label}"
      sed 's/^/      /' <<<"$output"
      echo
    else
      echo "PASS  ${label}"
    fi
  else
    FAILED=$((FAILED + 1))
    FAILED_NAMES+=("$label")
    echo "FAIL  ${label}"
    sed 's/^/      /' <<<"$output"
    echo
  fi
}

echo "shotkit checks, using $("$PYTHON" --version 2>&1)"
echo

# Preflight the two dependencies. Without this, a missing package turns one actionable
# line into fourteen identical failures and you have to read all of them to find out.
missing=""
"$PYTHON" -c 'import yaml' 2>/dev/null || missing="pyyaml"
"$PYTHON" -c 'import jsonschema' 2>/dev/null || missing="${missing:+$missing }jsonschema"
if [[ -n "$missing" ]]; then
  echo "Missing Python package(s): ${missing}" >&2
  echo >&2
  echo "  ${PYTHON} -m pip install ${missing}" >&2
  echo >&2
  echo "Then re-run ./tools/check.sh" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Structure and schemas
run "skills: frontmatter"            tools/validate_skills.py
run "schemas: are valid schemas"     tools/validate_schemas.py

# Capability matrix, including prose parity with the adapter files
run "capabilities: selftest"         tools/validate_capabilities.py --selftest
run "capabilities: matrix"           tools/validate_capabilities.py

# Brand-locks: packs allow templates, snapshots do not
run "brand-lock: selftest"           tools/validate_brand_lock.py --selftest
run "brand-lock: packs"              tools/validate_brand_lock.py \
  brand-packs/_template.md \
  brand-packs/whystrohm.md \
  brand-packs/examples/saas-clean.md \
  skills/brand-lock-extractor/examples/brand-lock.md
run "brand-lock: snapshots"          tools/validate_brand_lock.py --snapshots

# Storyboard instances, the rules JSON Schema cannot express
run "shots: selftest"                tools/validate_shots.py --selftest
run "shots: bundled examples"        tools/validate_shots.py --examples
run "shots: worked run"              tools/validate_shots.py \
  skills/visual-asset-critic/examples/worked-run

# Prompt files: the forge's hard rules, including verbatim series_lock anchors
run "prompts: selftest"              tools/validate_prompts.py --selftest
run "prompts: worked run"            tools/validate_prompts.py --examples

# Critique gate
run "critique: selftest"             tools/validate_critique.py --selftest
run "critique: fixtures"             tools/validate_critique.py --examples

# Provenance chain
run "provenance: selftest"           tools/validate_provenance.py --selftest
run "provenance: worked run"         tools/validate_provenance.py --examples --require-accept

# Tools that ship as part of the workflow
run "preview renderer: selftest"     tools/shots-to-html.py --selftest
run "prompt helper: selftest"        tools/copy-prompt.py --selftest

echo "─────────────────────────────────────────"
echo "${PASSED} passed, ${FAILED} failed"
if ((FAILED)); then
  printf 'failed: %s\n' "${FAILED_NAMES[@]}"
  exit 1
fi
exit 0

"""Copy a shot prompt from a shotkit prompts file to the system clipboard.

Handles both file shapes the forge writes: a full pass, and a revision file where each
shot block carries `# fix [...]` annotations above the prompt. Comment lines inside a
block are treated as annotations and never land in the clipboard, so what you paste
into a generator is the prompt and nothing else.

Usage:
  python tools/copy-prompt.py output/prompts/round-1/flux.txt
  python tools/copy-prompt.py output/prompts/round-2/revised-flux.txt --shot shot_02
  python tools/copy-prompt.py output/prompts/round-1/flux.txt --list
  python tools/copy-prompt.py --selftest
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# A shot block opens with the shot id near the start of a comment line. The forge's
# revision format prefixes it, so both of these are headers:
#   # shot_03, reframe, 11.0-16.0s, MCU eye-level push
#   # shot_03, promise, 3.0-8.0s, MCU eye-level push, revision (was REVISE)
#   # Revision of shot_03 (was REVISE)
SHOT_HEADER = re.compile(
    r"^#\s*(?:revision\s+of\s+)?(shot_\d{2,3})\b(.*)$", re.IGNORECASE
)
COMMENT_LINE = re.compile(r"^\s*#")

class Block:
    __slots__ = ("shot_id", "header", "annotations", "body")

def __init__(self, shot_id: str, header: str) -> None:
        self.shot_id = shot_id
        self.header = header
        self.annotations: list[str] = []
        self.body: list[str] = []

def prompt(self) -> str:
        return "\n".join(self.body).strip()

def parse_prompt_text(text: str) -> list[Block]:
    """Split a prompt file into shot blocks, separating annotations from prompt body."""
    blocks: list[Block] = []
    current: Block | None = None
return [b for b in blocks if b.prompt()]

def parse_prompt_file(path: Path) -> list[Block]:
    return parse_prompt_text(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

Two modes, because a brand-pack and a snapshot are not the same artifact.

A brand-pack (brand-packs/*.md) is a source document. An unfilled template is a legal
brand-pack: that is what a template is for.

A snapshot (brand-lock.snapshot.md, written into an output tree) is a provenance
record. It has to carry the header storyboard-architect promises to write, and if it
still contains template placeholders then the run it governs was built against nothing.
Pass --snapshot to check those extra rules, and --require-configured to reject
placeholders outright.

Required headings (case-insensitive, in any order):
- Identity, Palette, Typography, Mood adjectives, Never list,
  Aspect ratios, Color grade direction, Motion language, Voice rules

Required identity fields (under ## Identity):
- Brand, One-line description, Archetype, Voice posture

Usage:
    python tools/validate_brand_lock.py path/to/brand-lock.md [...]
    python tools/validate_brand_lock.py --snapshot path/to/brand-lock.snapshot.md
    python tools/validate_brand_lock.py --require-configured brand-packs/whystrohm.md
    python tools/validate_brand_lock.py --snapshots            # every bundled snapshot
    python tools/validate_brand_lock.py --selftest
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from _shotkit import (
    ISO_INSTANT_RE,
    PALETTE_ROLES,
    REPO_ROOT,
    is_unconfigured,
    parse_palette,

Schema validation alone is not enough: JSON Schema cannot express the cross-field
rules that make a verdict trustworthy. This validator adds them.

Gating invariant (the reason structured output exists):
  - Any 'blocking' issue      => verdict MUST be REJECT.
  - Three or more 'major'     => verdict MUST be REJECT.
  - One or two 'major'        => verdict MUST NOT be ACCEPT (caps at REVISE).
  - Therefore ACCEPT requires zero major/blocking issues.

Provenance invariant (version 1.1 and later):
  - A hash without its path, or a path without its hash, is not a reference.
  - image_ref must be present and non-null: a verdict about no image is not a verdict.
  - HIGH confidence requires the shot spec, the brand-lock, and the prompt to all be
    identified. The critic's own rubric says HIGH means all three were available.
  - generator, when named, must be an id in the capability matrix.

A critique that claims ACCEPT while carrying a blocking issue passes the schema but
FAILS here. So does a 1.1 critique that records an image hash and no image path.

Usage:
    python tools/validate_critique.py path/to/critique.json [...]
    python tools/validate_critique.py path/to/output-dir      # every critique in the tree
    python tools/validate_critique.py --examples              # bundled fixtures

This is the tool that answers "does this verdict still describe the file it reviewed."
Paths lie: a filename says nothing about the bytes behind it, so a frame regenerated
after its critique leaves every path reference intact and every claim about it wrong.
Content hashes are what make that detectable, and this walks them.

Checks:
  1. run.json validates against run.schema.json, and its run_id agrees with created_at.
  2. Rounds are numbered from 1 with no gaps and no duplicates.
  3. Every input hash in run.json still matches the file on disk. A brand-lock edited
     mid-project fails here instead of silently repointing the project's history.
  4. Every prompt hash recorded in run.json still matches the file on disk.
  5. Every critique validates against the schema and the gating invariant.
  6. Every critique's run_id matches run.json.
  7. Every critique's image, prompt, and brand-lock hashes match the files on disk.
  8. No two critiques cover the same shot in the same round. Two operators writing the
     same verdict path is a real conflict, not a silent overwrite.
  9. Every frame on disk has a critique for its round. An unreviewed frame is the
     failure mode where a re-roll slips past the gate on a stale ACCEPT.
 10. Every shot has at least one critique, and the latest verdict per shot is reported.
 11. Shots recorded as post_only still owe compositing work.

Exit status is 0 when the chain is intact. Add --require-accept to also demand that
every shot's latest verdict is ACCEPT, which is the pipeline stop condition made
executable rather than described.

    python tools/validate_provenance.py <output-dir> --require-accept

     a shot subject, shot ids out of chronological order, overlay fonts not named in
     the brand-lock typography section.

```markdown
## Composición básica

### Regla de tercios
- Divide el encuadre en una retícula de 3×3
- Coloca el sujeto en los puntos de intersección
- Sitúa el horizonte en la línea superior o inferior

### Líneas guía
- Usa líneas para conducir la mirada
- Caminos, ríos, barandales
- Que apunten al sujeto

### Encuadre dentro del encuadre
- Enmarca al sujeto con elementos del primer plano
- Marcos de puerta, ventanas, ramas
- Aporta capas y profundidad

### Simetría y equilibrio
- Simetría perfecta = estabilidad, solemnidad
- Asimetría = dinamismo, tensión
- Equilibra el peso visual

### Espacio negativo
- El vacío refuerza el punto focal
- Da "espacio para respirar" al sujeto
- Estética minimalista
```

```markdown
## Tipos de plano — Shot Types

### Plano general (Wide Shot)
- Establece la escena
- Muestra el entorno
- El personaje se ve pequeño

### Plano entero (Full Shot)
- Cuerpo completo
- Acción legible
- Luce el vestuario

- De la cintura hacia arriba
- Escenas de diálogo
- Gestualidad de manos

### Primer plano (Close-up)
- De los hombros hacia arriba
- Expresión emocional
- Línea de diálogo importante

- Detalle de ojos o manos
- Emoción intensa
- Detalle de objeto
```

texto: ## Fundamentos de animación

encabezado: Creación Visual — Visual Media › Fundamentos de animación › Los 12 principios
texto: ### Los 12 principios

encabezado: Creación Visual — Visual Media › Fundamentos de animación › Los 12 principios
texto:
```markdown
## Los 12 principios de animación de Disney

1. **Squash & Stretch** (compresión y estiramiento)
   - Conservar el volumen
   - Comunicar peso y elasticidad

2. **Anticipación** (Anticipation)
   - Agacharse antes de saltar
   - Retraer el brazo antes del golpe

3. **Puesta en escena** (Staging)
   - Comunicar la intención con claridad
   - Guiar la mirada del espectador

4. **Directo vs. pose a pose** (Straight Ahead & Pose to Pose)
   - Directo: fluido, orgánico
   - Pose a pose: preciso, controlable

5. **Acción continuada y superpuesta** (Follow Through & Overlapping)
   - El retardo del cabello y la ropa
   - Aporta naturalidad

6. **Entradas y salidas lentas** (Slow In & Slow Out)
   - El movimiento arranca y termina lento
   - Y acelera en medio

7. **Arcos** (Arcs)
   - El movimiento natural es curvo
   - Evita la sensación mecánica

8. **Acción secundaria** (Secondary Action)
   - Micromovimientos además de la acción principal
   - Enriquecen al personaje

9. **Timing** (Timing)
   - El número de cuadros define la velocidad
   - Afecta la sensación de peso

10. **Exageración** (Exaggeration)
    - Más intenso que la realidad
    - Resalta el rasgo distintivo

11. **Dibujo sólido** (Solid Drawing)
    - Entender la estructura tridimensional
    - Peso y equilibrio

12. **Atractivo** (Appeal)
    - Carisma del personaje
    - Que dé ganas de verlo
```

texto:
```markdown
## Principios de edición

### Corte en movimiento
- Cambia de plano durante la acción
- Mantiene la fluidez

### Corte en reposo
- Cambia durante una pausa
- Habitual en escenas de diálogo

### Regla de los 180 grados
- Conserva la posición relativa de los personajes
- Evita cruzar el eje

### J-Cut / L-Cut
- J-Cut: el audio entra antes que la imagen
- L-Cut: la imagen se mantiene después del audio
- Aumentan la fluidez
```

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge
texto: # Visual Prompt Forge

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge
texto: You are turning structured shot data into prompts that work in production. Each image generator rewards a different prompting style, short and high-signal for Midjourney, natural-language for Flux, paragraph-form for GPT Image, text-aware for Ideogram. A prompt that crushes in one will produce slop in another.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › What you produce
texto:
Round 1 is the first pass. Revision mode writes `output/prompts/round-2/`, and so on.
The round in the path is not decoration: prompt files used to be written to one fixed
path per generator, so round 2 destroyed round 1 and the prompt that actually produced
most of the surviving frames was gone.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › What you produce
texto: Each file is plain text, one prompt per shot, separated by a blank line and a `# shot_NN` comment. Designed for copy-paste workflows, drop into the generator's UI or pipe into an API.

texto: ## The five-layer prompt anatomy

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › The five-layer prompt anatomy
texto: Every prompt is composed from these layers. Read `references/prompt-anatomy.md` for the full theory. Quick version:

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › The five-layer prompt anatomy
texto: 1. **Brand Lock**, palette, type, mood, "never" list (constant across project)

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › The five-layer prompt anatomy
texto: 2. **Series Lock**, character/environment/lighting anchors (constant across storyboard)

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › The five-layer prompt anatomy

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › The five-layer prompt anatomy
texto: 4. **Text Layer**, **never in the prompt**, composited separately

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › The five-layer prompt anatomy
texto: 5. **Generator Adapter**, model-specific syntax wrapper

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › The five-layer prompt anatomy
texto: The first four come from `shots.json` and the brand-lock. The fifth is what this skill applies.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters
texto: Each adapter file documents the prompting style, parameter syntax, and known pitfalls for that generator. You **must** read the adapter before writing prompts for it. Don't guess from training data, image-gen syntax has churned multiple times.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters
texto: **`adapters/_capabilities.json` is the single source of truth for per-generator limits** (`max_prompt_words`, `supports_text_render`, `supports_motion`, `aspect_param`, and so on). Read it once at the start and respect those values when composing, and do not target motion on a stills-only generator.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters
texto:
`max_prompt_words` is a ceiling. The range in an adapter `.md` is the recommended target
and always sits inside that ceiling, so a `.md` saying "40 to 70 words" under a ceiling of
120 is guidance, not a conflict. Where a fact in a `.md` and a fact in the JSON genuinely
disagree, **the JSON wins**.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 2. Pick the adapters
texto:
That rule is now enforced rather than trusted. `tools/validate_capabilities.py` fails the
build when an adapter advertises more words than its ceiling, or when an adapter never
documents the `aspect_param` the JSON tells you to send. The second check exists because
nano-banana's matrix entry said `aspect_ratio` while its adapter said the API expects
`aspectRatio`; the precedence rule meant the wrong one won, silently, on every prompt.

texto: 1. Pull brand-lock palette, mood, "never" list

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 3. Compose per shot
texto: 2. Pull series_lock character/environment/lighting

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 3. Compose per shot
texto: 3. Pull shot framing/angle/motion/subject

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 3. Compose per shot
texto: 4. **Strip any on_screen_text reference**, text never goes in the prompt

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 3. Compose per shot
texto: 5. Apply the generator adapter's syntax wrapper

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 3. Compose per shot
texto: 6. Append generator-specific parameters (aspect ratio, style flags, seed if applicable)

Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4. Write output files
texto:
The `#` lines are comments; the user copies just the prompt body. `tools/copy-prompt.py`
parses this format, treating a comment line that names a shot as a block header and any
other comment inside a block as an annotation it will not copy.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4. Write output files
texto:
Record the run and round in the header, not a wall-clock "Generated" line. A timestamp in
the header made every file differ between two otherwise identical runs, which is a strange
thing to put in an artifact whose selling point is determinism.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4b. Append the round to run.json
texto: ### Step 4b. Append the round to run.json

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4b. Append the round to run.json
texto:
After writing the files, append an entry to `run.json`'s `rounds` array: the round number,
`started_at`, a `reason`, and for each file its generator, path, SHA-256, and the shot ids
it covers.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4b. Append the round to run.json
texto:
```bash
shasum -a 256 output/prompts/round-1/*.txt
```

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 4b. Append the round to run.json
texto:
This is the only writeable part of `run.json`. Everything else was fixed when the
architect wrote it.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 5. Hand off
texto: ### Step 5. Hand off

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 5. Hand off
texto: Tell the user where the files are. Offer the next step:

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 5. Hand off
texto: > "Want me to QA the generated images against the storyboard? Use `visual-asset-critic` once you have the renders."

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 5. Hand off
texto: For paste-into-generator workflows, the user can pipe individual shots to the clipboard with the bundled helper:

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 5. Hand off
texto:
```bash
python tools/copy-prompt.py output/prompts/round-1/midjourney.txt
python tools/copy-prompt.py output/prompts/round-2/revised-midjourney.txt --shot shot_03
```

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Workflow › Step 5. Hand off
texto: This is optional. The `.txt` files are also directly readable, and the user can copy any block by hand. The helper exists for the case where the operator is bouncing between the terminal and a generator UI repeatedly.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop)
texto: ## Revision mode (closing the QA loop)

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop)
texto: This is what `visual-asset-critic`'s structured output is for. When the user hands you `shots.json` plus one or more `critique.json` files (the machine-readable verdict the critic writes), don't re-forge the whole storyboard, re-emit prompts for **only the shots that failed**, with the fix already applied.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Trigger
texto: ### Trigger

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Trigger
texto: The user says "apply the critique", "revise the failed shots", "re-roll what didn't pass", or hands over an output tree containing `critiques/`.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto: ### Workflow

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto:
1. Read every critique under `output/critiques/round-{N}/`, where N is the highest round
   present. Each file is one shot's verdict (`shot_id`, `verdict`, `issues[]`).

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto: 2. Skip any with `verdict: ACCEPT`. Those are done.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto:
3. **Stop on `REJECT`.** A REJECT means the critic found a blocking issue, or three or more
   major ones: a failure with no clear fix path. Re-emitting a prompt for it pretends
   otherwise. List the rejected shots, say what the critic said about them, and ask the
   user how to proceed. Common answers are a change to the shot spec, a change to the
   brand-lock, or a different generator, and all three are decisions above this skill's
   pay grade.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto: 4. For every `REVISE` shot, walk its `issues[]` and branch on `fix_type`:

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto:
- **`prompt-level`**, recompose that shot's prompt with the change in `fix` applied
     (e.g. add the missing series_lock anchor). Re-emit it.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto:
- **`re-roll`**, keep the prompt identical; the generation was just a bad sample.
     Re-emit it with a `# fix [Technical, re-roll]` annotation saying to take 2-3 samples
     and pick the cleanest.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto:
- **`post-level`**, do **not** re-emit. The fix happens in compositing, not a new
     generation.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto:
5. A shot whose issues are all `post-level` needs no new prompt. Leave it out of the
   revised file and add its id to `post_only_shots` on the new round entry in `run.json`.
   Saying it in chat is not recording it: that obligation has to exist on disk or the
   compositing step is a memory.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Workflow
texto: 6. Re-apply the five-layer anatomy and the same adapter as the original run.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Output
texto: ### Output

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Output
texto:
Write `output/prompts/round-{N+1}/revised-{generator}.txt` containing only the revised
shots, then append the round to `run.json`. Annotate each shot with what changed and why,
citing the issue:

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Output
texto:
```
# shot_03, reframe, 11.0-16.0s, MCU eye-level push, revision (was REVISE)
# fix [Series Lock, major]: added 'salt-and-pepper hair' to the character anchor (was missing)
# fix [Shot Spec, minor]: medium shot -> medium close-up
{the revised prompt}
```

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Output
texto:
The block header leads with the shot id, same as a full pass. `tools/copy-prompt.py`
identifies a block by the shot id near the start of the line, so a header that led with
"Revision of" produced a file the paste helper could not read at all, which is
inconvenient in the one file the operator is about to paste from repeatedly.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Output
texto:
Tell the user which shots were revised, which need only post work, which were rejected,
and which were already ACCEPT. Then they generate the revised shots and run
`visual-asset-critic` again.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Determinism, and its limits
texto: ### Determinism, and its limits

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Determinism, and its limits
texto:
Given the same `shots.json`, the same brand-lock, and the same critique, this should
produce the same revised prompt. Nothing in the file format fights that any more: no
wall-clock stamps, no random ordering.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Revision mode (closing the QA loop) › Determinism, and its limits
texto:
What the format cannot guarantee is the judgement in between. Applying a `fix` field means
reading a sentence of English and editing prose, so hold yourself to the narrowest edit
that satisfies the fix and leave every other layer byte-identical. If you find yourself
rewriting a prompt the critique did not ask you to touch, stop: that is drift, and it will
read as a mystery six shots later.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules
texto: ## Hard rules

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules
texto: These are non-negotiable. Violating them produces broken output even if the prompt looks fine.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 1. Text is never in the prompt
texto: ### Rule 1. Text is never in the prompt

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 1. Text is never in the prompt
texto: If the shot has `on_screen_text: "text_03"`, the prompt does NOT contain the text content. Text is composited separately. The only exception: Ideogram, where text-in-image is the reason you'd choose it, but even then, treat it as an explicit override flagged in rationale.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 2. Brand colors never in shot subject prose
texto: ### Rule 2. Brand colors never in shot subject prose

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 2. Brand colors never in shot subject prose
texto: Colors come from the series_lock color_grade and the brand_lock palette. They get rendered into the prompt by the adapter. Don't write "deep navy blazer" in the shot subject if "deep navy" is already in the palette, that's a duplicated description and produces oversaturation.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
texto: ### Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
texto:
The series_lock `environment`, `lighting`, and `color_grade` strings flow into every
prompt **verbatim**. This is what produces visual consistency across shots. If you
paraphrase or vary, shots stop matching each other.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
texto:
Verbatim means the whole string, unedited. Not "the same idea in better prose". The
failure mode is specific and easy to walk into: you are writing fluent descriptive
English, `environment` is "minimalist home office, white walls, oak desk, single
houseplant", and it reads more naturally as "a minimal home office with white walls and
an oak desk". That is drift. The frames stop matching, and it stays invisible until you
line up six shots and see six different rooms.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
texto:
Capitalising the first letter to start a sentence is fine, because the check is
case-insensitive. "Minimalist home office, white walls, oak desk, single houseplant."
satisfies the rule and reads like a sentence. Nothing else may change: no reordering, no
dropped clause, no synonym, no inserted adjective.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
texto:
`character` is a warning rather than an error, because a shot with no person in it can
legitimately leave it out. When the shot has a person, it is verbatim too.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
texto: This rule is enforced now, not trusted:

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
texto:
```bash
python tools/validate_prompts.py output/
```

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 3. Series_lock anchors are verbatim
texto:
It exists because a careful authoring pass over a seven-shot storyboard drifted on these
anchors in all seven shots while every other validator stayed green.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 4. Adapters are the source of truth on syntax
texto: ### Rule 4. Adapters are the source of truth on syntax

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 4. Adapters are the source of truth on syntax
texto: If your training data says Midjourney uses `--style 4a` and the adapter file says `--style raw`, the adapter wins. Image-gen syntax changes monthly. The adapter is current; your training is not.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
texto: ### Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
texto: A prompt can be beautifully written and still be impossible to shoot. Every prompt declares, before anything else:

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
texto: - **Where the body sits in frame.** Which third it occupies. On a piece that composites two eras with a vertical mask, a body sitting on the centre line gets split in half and no amount of post fixes it. This is the single most expensive failure in the kit, and it is invisible until the mask goes on.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
texto: - **The point of view.** Profile, frontal, side, rear. "A man walking" is not a shot.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
texto: - **The direction of travel.** Left to right, right to left, toward camera. Without it the generator picks, and consecutive shots stop matching.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
texto: - **Nothing that contradicts the camera.** A subject who walks away from camera cannot also keep the same size in frame.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
texto: - **Handedness in any two-person contact.** If one raises a hand, name which one, or you get two right hands meeting.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 6. Shot logic before shot poetry
texto: - **No brand marks.** Logos and lettering are composited in post. Generators deform them.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 5. Prompts must be reproducible
texto: ### Rule 5. Prompts must be reproducible

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Hard rules › Rule 5. Prompts must be reproducible
texto: Every prompt is composed from the same inputs the same way. If two consecutive runs produce different prompts for the same shot, the skill is broken. Determinism is the whole point.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto: ## Quality bar

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto: Run the validator. Do not eyeball this list.

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto:
```bash
python tools/validate_prompts.py output/
python tools/copy-prompt.py output/prompts/round-1/flux.txt --list
```

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto:
`validate_prompts.py` checks the mechanical half, which is everything that used to be a
checkbox here:

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto: - the header names the storyboard, generator, aspect, brand-lock, run, and round

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto: - the generator is a real id in `_capabilities.json`

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto: - the header aspect matches `project.aspect`

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto: - no prompt exceeds that generator's `max_prompt_words` ceiling

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto: - a full pass covers every shot; a revision file covers a subset of real shots

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto: - no shot block is duplicated, and none has a header with no body

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto: - **Rule 1**: no on-screen text copy appears in any prompt

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto:
- **Rule 3**: `environment`, `lighting`, and `color_grade` appear verbatim, with the
  character anchor as a warning

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto:
- **Rule 6**: every shot states which third of the frame the body occupies, its point of
  view and its direction of travel; no scale contradictions, no two people at the same
  frame edge, no unnamed handedness in a two-person contact, no brand marks in frame

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto: What it cannot check, and you still have to:

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto: - [ ] One output file per requested generator

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto:
- [ ] On a revision pass, the shots you left out are accounted for as ACCEPT, post-only,
      or rejected, and you said which is which

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto: - [ ] Generator-specific parameters are right for the surface the user will paste into

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto: - [ ] The round is appended to `run.json` with a hash per prompt file

encabezado: Visual Prompt Forge › Quality bar
texto: - [ ] The prompt actually describes the shot, which is the part no validator will ever do

encabezado: Adapter: Hailuo 02 Pro (motion-aware video, budget iteration)
texto: Hailuo 02 Pro is the cheap, fast iteration model. Strong motion response and prompt-following for the price, on fal.ai. Use it to **find the shot**, block out camera move, framing, and timing across many quick drafts, then re-generate the keeper on Kling (motion finals), Veo (dialogue), or Seedance (sequences). Treat Hailuo output as a working draft, not a final asset.

texto: ## Iteration workflow

encabezado: Adapter: Hailuo 02 Pro (motion-aware video, budget iteration) › Iteration workflow
texto: 1. Draft the shot on Hailuo with `prompt_optimizer=false`. Cheap, fast.

encabezado: Adapter: Hailuo 02 Pro (motion-aware video, budget iteration) › Iteration workflow
texto: 2. Lock the camera move, framing, and timing that read best.

encabezado: Adapter: Hailuo 02 Pro (motion-aware video, budget iteration) › Iteration workflow
texto: 3. Re-generate the keeper on the right final-tier model: **Kling** for motion finals, **Veo** for dialogue/lipsync, **Seedance** for multi-shot sequences.

encabezado: Adapter: Hailuo 02 Pro (motion-aware video, budget iteration) › Iteration workflow
texto: 4. Carry the exact prompt forward, the adapters share the same five-layer anatomy, so the prompt body ports with only parameter changes.

encabezado: Adapter: Hailuo 02 Pro (motion-aware video, budget iteration) › Example
texto: ## Example

encabezado: Adapter: Hailuo 02 Pro (motion-aware video, budget iteration) › Example
texto: **Draft of the `motion = "push"` shot.**

encabezado: Adapter: Hailuo 02 Pro (motion-aware video, budget iteration) › Example
texto:
```
Camera dollies forward slowly at a steady pace. A founder in his mid-thirties with salt-and-pepper hair in a navy crewneck sits at his laptop in a minimalist home office and leans slightly forward toward window light off-camera left. Soft natural side-light, warm afternoon. Warm filmic color grade, muted teal shadows. Calm operator mood.
```

encabezado: Adapter: Hailuo 02 Pro (motion-aware video, budget iteration) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: ## Pitfalls to avoid

encabezado: Adapter: Hailuo 02 Pro (motion-aware video, budget iteration) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't ship Hailuo drafts as finals.** Re-roll the keeper on a final-tier model.

encabezado: Adapter: Hailuo 02 Pro (motion-aware video, budget iteration) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't enable the prompt optimizer for series work.** Auto-rewrite breaks shot-to-shot consistency.

encabezado: Adapter: Hailuo 02 Pro (motion-aware video, budget iteration) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't stack two camera moves.** One move per shot.

encabezado: Adapter: Hailuo 02 Pro (motion-aware video, budget iteration) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't include text content.** Composite captions in post.

encabezado: Adapter: Hailuo 02 Pro (motion-aware video, budget iteration) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't over-polish the draft prompt.** Spend words on motion and framing; save the photographic detail for the final-tier re-roll.

encabezado: Adapter: Hailuo 02 Pro (motion-aware video, budget iteration) › Output handoff
texto: ## Output handoff

encabezado: Adapter: Hailuo 02 Pro (motion-aware video, budget iteration) › Output handoff
texto: Hailuo output is a draft used to choose the shot. The deliverable comes from the final-tier re-roll. If a Hailuo take is genuinely good enough to keep, treat it like any other clip: editorial assembly, text-overlay compositing, color grade, audio.

texto: # Adapter: Ideogram (v3)

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3)
texto: > Capability data (length ceiling, text/motion support, aspect param) is canonical in `_capabilities.json`. This file is the how-to-prompt guidance. `max_prompt_words` there is a ceiling; the range below is the recommended target and has to sit inside it. Where a fact here and a fact in the JSON disagree, the JSON wins, and `tools/validate_capabilities.py` fails the build instead of letting the two drift.

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3)
texto: Ideogram is the only generator that reliably renders text inside images. Use it for cases where text-as-image is the deliverable, posters, branded social tiles, signage, packaging mockups. For everything else, default to Flux or Midjourney and composite text separately.

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3)
texto: This adapter has **two modes**: composited (default) and text-in-image (override).

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Mode 1: Composited (default)
texto: ## Mode 1: Composited (default)

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Mode 1: Composited (default)
texto: Same as Flux, generate the image clean, composite text in post. Use when Ideogram is being chosen for general image quality, not text rendering. Syntax matches Flux conventions.

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Mode 2: Text-in-image (override)
texto: ## Mode 2: Text-in-image (override)

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Mode 2: Text-in-image (override)
texto: Use when the on-screen text is meant to appear as part of the image itself, a poster headline, a sign in the scene, a packaging label. This is the only case where a generator prompt contains the text content.

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Mode 2: Text-in-image (override)
texto: **To trigger Mode 2, the shot must have an explicit override flag in rationale**, e.g.:

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Mode 2: Text-in-image (override)
texto:
```
"rationale": "Text-in-image override: poster shot, headline must render as part of composition"
```

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Mode 2: Text-in-image (override)
texto: If you don't see that override flag, default to Mode 1.

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Syntax pattern (Mode 2)
texto: ## Syntax pattern (Mode 2)

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Syntax pattern (Mode 2)
Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Syntax pattern (Mode 2)
texto: The exact text must be in straight double-quotes. Ideogram parses these as the text-render target.

texto: ## Length

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Length
texto:
Ideogram handles **60–120 words** comfortably. Text-bearing prompts run shorter still:
the more scene description you stack around a text instruction, the more likely the
render drops or garbles the copy.

texto: ## Composition pattern (Mode 1, composited)

texto: Same as Flux pattern, no text in prompt:

texto:
```
{Framing description with character and action}. {Environment from series_lock}. {Lighting from series_lock}. {Photographic spec}. {Brand mood and color}. Clean composition with negative space for text overlay placement.
```

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Composition pattern (Mode 2, text-in-image)


**Shot:** poster-style hero frame, brand launch
**Brand-lock:** display font is `Inter Black`, headline color `#0F1F3A` on `#F5F0E8` cream background
**Text content:** `built different`

```
Editorial poster composition, dense cream background, single bold composition. Minimalist studio environment, even diffused lighting. The text "built different" appears center of the frame, in heavy sans-serif typography (Inter Black style), color deep navy #0F1F3A on cream #F5F0E8 background. Calm, considered, operator brand mood, confident without shouting.
```

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › When NOT to use Ideogram
texto: ## When NOT to use Ideogram

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › When NOT to use Ideogram
texto: - **Photorealistic scenes with people**. Flux is better

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › When NOT to use Ideogram
texto: - **Cinematic mood/aesthetic**. Midjourney is better

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › When NOT to use Ideogram
texto: - **Product photography**. Flux 2 Pro is better

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › When NOT to use Ideogram
texto: - **Series work where consistency matters**. Midjourney with `--cref` or Flux with seed-locking handles consistency better

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › When NOT to use Ideogram
texto: Ideogram's specialty is text. If the brief doesn't need text-in-image, picking Ideogram is choosing the wrong tool.

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: ## Pitfalls to avoid

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't use Mode 2 without the rationale override**, defaults to text-in-image cause double-text (composited + generated) which destroys the comp

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't trust magic_prompt**, it auto-rewrites and produces inconsistent shots across a series

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't pile multiple text elements in one prompt**. Ideogram handles one text element well, two becomes lottery, three is broken

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't use cursive/decorative fonts**, even Ideogram fails on these. Sans-serif and clean serif are reliable

encabezado: Adapter: Ideogram (v3) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't forget seed**, for any series work, lock the seed at the storyboard level

texto: # Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video)

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video)
texto: > Capability data (length ceiling, text/motion support, aspect param) is canonical in `_capabilities.json`. This file is the how-to-prompt guidance. `max_prompt_words` there is a ceiling; the range below is the recommended target and has to sit inside it. Where a fact here and a fact in the JSON disagree, the JSON wins, and `tools/validate_capabilities.py` fails the build instead of letting the two drift.

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video)
texto: Kling 3.0 generates short video clips, not still frames. It is the default motion model: the best camera-motion realism per dollar on fal.ai, and the strongest image-to-video of the four. Reach for it first. Escalate to Veo (dialogue/lipsync), Seedance (multi-shot), or Hailuo (cheap iteration) only when the shot needs what Kling does not do.

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video)
texto: With video the **camera motion becomes load-bearing** instead of optional. The same shot generates differently when `motion` is `static` versus `push` versus `handheld`. Use this adapter when the storyboard is destined for video generation rather than still-frame compositing.

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Syntax pattern
texto: ## Syntax pattern

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Syntax pattern
Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Syntax pattern
texto: Camera motion goes **first**. This is the inverse of image generators where camera is implied. With video the camera's behaviour is the first thing the model must understand.

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Parameters
texto: ## Parameters

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Parameters
texto: | Parameter | Default | Notes |

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Parameters
Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Parameters
texto: | `duration` | `5s` for shots, `10s` for hero | 5s and 10s are the supported lengths |

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Parameters
texto: | `aspect_ratio` | from `project.aspect` | |

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Parameters
texto: | `cfg_scale` | `0.5` | Lower = looser/more dynamic, higher = closer to prompt |

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Parameters
texto: | `start_image` | optional | Image-to-video. Pass an accepted still from `shots.json` assets to lock the opening frame |

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Parameters
texto: | `tail_image` | optional | End-frame target for controlled moves |

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Parameters
texto: | `negative_prompt` | per series | Supported. Use to suppress drift, e.g. `extra fingers, warped face` |

```
{prompt}
```

texto: ## Length

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Length
texto: Kling handles **80–150 words** comfortably. Motion description adds a beat over a still prompt; do not pad past it.

texto: ## Motion vocabulary

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Motion vocabulary

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Subject motion
texto: ## Subject motion

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Subject motion
texto: Beyond the camera, describe what the subject does over the duration:

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Subject motion
texto: > "Over the course of the shot the founder leans slightly forward and turns his face toward the window light off-camera left."

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Subject motion
texto: Static composition is not enough for video. This is what separates a video prompt from an image prompt.

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Example
texto: ## Example

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Example
texto: **Same shot data as the image-adapter examples, with `motion = "push"`.**

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Example
texto:
```
Camera dollies forward slowly into the scene at a steady pace. A founder in his mid-thirties with salt-and-pepper hair, wearing a navy crewneck, sits at his laptop in a minimalist home office; over the shot he leans slightly forward and his face turns toward window light off-camera left, holding negative space on the right of frame throughout. Soft natural side-light from a large window, warm afternoon golden hour. Shot on a 50mm prime equivalent, shallow depth of field. Warm filmic color grade with muted teal shadows. Calm, considered, operator mood.
```

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Continuity across shots
texto: ## Continuity across shots

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Continuity across shots
texto: - Use `start_image` from the previous shot's accepted final frame to chain a sequence.

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Continuity across shots
texto: - Repeat the series_lock character anchor verbatim in every prompt.

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Continuity across shots
texto: - Do not flip lighting direction between consecutive shots (window-left stays window-left).

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Continuity across shots
texto: - Even with start-frame locking, each clip is a fresh generation. Plan for an editorial pass.

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: ## Pitfalls to avoid

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't put camera motion at the end.** Kling parses motion best as the leading instruction.

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't request multiple camera moves in one shot.** Pick one; compound moves break.

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't describe motion faster than the duration allows.** A slow dolly over 5s is plausible; over 1s it is jitter.

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't include text content.** Video text rendering is unreliable; composite or animate text in post.

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't expect frame-perfect character match between clips.** Budget editorial cleanup.

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Output handoff
texto: ## Output handoff

encabezado: Adapter: Kling 3.0 (motion-aware video) › Output handoff
texto: Generated clips are raw material, not deliverable. After generation they still need: editorial assembly to storyboard timing, text-overlay compositing from `text-overlays.json`, a color-grade pass, and audio (VO, music, sound design). Say this in handoff.

encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image)
texto: Google's Nano Banana model (`gemini-2.5-flash-image`) is the edit-and-iterate champion. Where other generators are best for first-frame creation, Nano Banana excels at variations, inpainting, and reference-based modification. The 2026 production pattern is to generate hero frames in Midjourney or Flux, then use Nano Banana for variants.

encabezado: Adapter: Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image)
texto: For storyboard work, Nano Banana is the right choice when you need **many variations of a single concept** or you're feeding generated images back through for refinement.
